title: PREVENTION-EPIC: Stop drift + compounding debt before workers re-create it
description:
## Why this epic exists
The 2026-04-30 audit (`calmly-3py`) found 22 items of bugs/drift produced by ~12 autonomous-worker commits. The drift signature was textbook autonomous-worker behavior:

- Two workers each invented `tasks/repo.ts` helpers locally instead of grepping for existing ones
- Row types redefined four ways because workers default to "redeclare for safety"
- `Triage.tsx` grew to 880 LOC because no per-file budget existed
- Schema columns added to one of three places (shared/server/desktop) without the others
- Inconsistent error contracts (`NotFound` vs `InvalidArgs` vs `InvalidUntil`) because no enforced vocabulary
- New pages shipped without e2e because no "ship-with-tests" gate

This epic is the **prevention layer**. Each child addresses a *category* of failure mode the audit catalogued, with the goal that the next audit finds materially less.

## Levers (ordered by cost-to-leverage ratio)

### 1. Worker prompt hardening (cheapest, biggest immediate impact)
Update `.ralph/prompts/{opus,sonnet}.md` and `.ralph/AGENT.md` with: grep-before-write rule, kit reference for established primitives, schema-touch rule, LOC budget. Single-PR text edit; halves drift.

### 2. CI gates (medium cost, durable)
ESLint `max-lines`, banned literal enum strings, schema-parity test, mandatory e2e on PRs, migrations-touch-shared rule. Each gate addresses a specific drift pattern from the audit.

### 3. Architectural — codegen migrations from shared schemas
Higher cost; eliminates a whole bug class. P3 explore.

### 4. Cadence — recurring audit agent
Schedule a routine to re-run the three-pronged audit every 50 worker commits or 2 weeks. Auto-files findings under a new `*-audit-YYYY-MM-DD` epic.

## Hard rule for workers
**Children of this epic land alongside `calmly-3py` audit fixes — not after.** Otherwise we'll fix the audit findings only to have workers re-create them in parallel commits. The worker-prompt hardening child especially must close before the loop relaunches.

## Acceptance
- All 🔴 children closed before next worker relaunch
- All 🟠 children landed within 1 week of relaunch
- Re-audit (cadence child) shows < 5 findings of the same patterns

## References
- Source audit: `calmly-3py` and the agent reports in the 2026-04-30 conversation
- Affected files inventoried per child
close_reason: Closed

title: PREVENT-1: Harden ralph worker prompts (grep-before-write, kit reference, LOC budget, schema rule)
description:
## Why
The 2026-04-30 audit found that **two workers each invented the same `tasks/repo.ts` helpers** because their prompts said "match existing patterns" but never said "grep first". Same root cause for: 4× row type redefinitions, 4× LoadingShell duplications, 3× formatRelative copies, inconsistent error codes.

This is a 30-minute text edit to `.ralph/` that probably halves the next audit's findings. Land before relaunching the loop.

## Work — concrete edits

### A. Add a "Before you write code" section to `.ralph/PROMPT.md`
Insert *before* the "When you're stuck" section:

```
## Before you write code (anti-drift rules)

These rules exist because past workers re-created helpers, types, and
patterns that already lived elsewhere in the repo. Each is a hard rule.

1. **Grep before write.** Before creating a util, hook, helper, or row
   interface, run `Grep` for:
   - The function name you're about to write (and 2 nearby aliases)
   - The shape of the data (e.g. `interface TaskRow`, `type InboxItem`)
   - Any error code string you're about to introduce
   If a match exists, *use it* or extend it. If you find near-duplicates
   in 2+ files, that is a refactor opportunity — file a bd issue and
   stop.

2. **Use the kit.** See `.ralph/AGENT.md` § "Established primitives" for
   the canonical components/helpers. Build new pages using them. If a
   page can't use the kit, write a 1-line note in the bead explaining
   why.

3. **Schema touches all three places or none.** Any change to a
   sync-replicated column updates `shared/src/model/<x>.ts` AND the
   matching `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/*.sql` AND
   `server/migrations/*.cjs`. Diffs that touch only one will fail
   review.

4. **LOC budget: 300 lines per file.** If your edit pushes a file past
   300, stop. File a "split this file" bd issue first, close it, then
   come back. (`Triage.tsx` hit 880 lines under the old rule — never
   again.)

5. **Error vocabulary lives in `shared/src/errors.ts`.** Don't invent
   new error codes inline. If you need a new one, add it to the union
   there first.

6. **Ship with tests.** Every IPC handler ships with happy + auth-fail +
   bad-payload tests. Every renderer page ships with at least one e2e
   spec covering the golden path. No exceptions; if test infra is
   missing, file a P1 bead and block on it.
```

### B. Add an "Established primitives" section to `.ralph/AGENT.md`
*Note: this section's content depends on `calmly-3py.5/6/7/8/13/15/17` landing first. List primitives as they ship.*

```
## Established primitives — use these, don't reinvent

UI:
- `<PageStateView state={...} ready={...} />` — loading/error/sign-out
  shell. Replaces inline LoadingShell + FailureNotice.
- `useResource(fetcher, deps)` — page-data hook. Returns the
  discriminated union PageStateView consumes.
- `formatRelative(when, now?)`, `formatClock(when, opts?)` —
  `desktop/src/renderer/utils/time.ts`
- `snoozeOneHour`, `snoozeTomorrowMorning`, `snoozeNextWeek` —
  `desktop/src/renderer/utils/snooze.ts`

IPC (main):
- `defineAuthedHandler(channel, schema, fn)` —
  `desktop/src/main/ipc/handler.ts`. All new IPC handlers use this.
  Local `isStringId()` and inline payload validation are forbidden.
- Task row helpers: `loadTask`, `enqueueTaskUpsert`, `TaskRow`,
  `SCHEDULABLE_STATUSES` from `desktop/src/main/tasks/repo.ts`

Types:
- All sync-replicated row types live in `@calmly/shared` or are
  re-exported from main stores via `desktop/src/preload/api-types.ts`.
  Don't redeclare row interfaces in renderer or preload.
- Status/source/role enums import from `@calmly/shared`. No literal
  unions like `"open" | "in_progress"` outside that package.

Error codes:
- Defined in `shared/src/errors.ts`. Use these constants, don't write
  string literals.
```

### C. Tighten the priority bucket guidance in `prompts/{opus,sonnet}.md`
Add to each, after the "Your specialty" section:

```
## File-touch awareness
Before claiming a bead, run `git log --oneline -10 ralph/<other>` and
read the last 3 commits' file lists. If your bead touches the same
files the other worker is actively editing, skip it — race conditions
between workers cost more than parallelism saves. The merge loop will
expose the conflict; better to serialize.
```

### D. Add to opus.md
After "Decompose aggressively":

```
- **Audit your own diff before closing.** Before `bd close`, run:
  - `wc -l <files-you-touched>` — any > 300 LOC? File a split issue.
  - `Grep` for any new helper name you wrote — 2+ hits means you
    duplicated; consolidate.
  - `git diff --stat` — touching `migrations/` without a matching
    `shared/` edit? Add the schema or revert.
```

## Files
- `.ralph/PROMPT.md`
- `.ralph/AGENT.md`
- `.ralph/prompts/opus.md`
- `.ralph/prompts/sonnet.md`

## Acceptance
- All four files updated as above
- Manually walk through one of the 22 audit findings (e.g. duplicated `loadTask`) and verify the new prompt rules would have prevented it
- Commit and `git push` so the next worker iteration picks up the new prompts (workers read these from the worktree, not from a cached version)

## Severity rationale
P0 — must close before the worker loop relaunches. Otherwise we ship `calmly-3py` fixes only to watch the next 12 commits re-create the same patterns. Filed under audit-2026-04-30.
close_reason: Closed

title: PREVENT-2: ESLint rules — max-lines, banned-enum-literals, no-duplicate-shapes
description:
## Why
The audit found three patterns that an ESLint config could have stopped at commit time:
1. **`Triage.tsx` hit 880 LOC** because no max-lines rule. Workers don't proactively split.
2. **Status/source string literals scattered across 4+ files** because no rule banned them. `"open" | "in_progress" | ...` redefined inline instead of importing from `@calmly/shared`.
3. **Row types redeclared in renderer and preload** instead of re-exported. A custom rule could flag interface declarations whose shape near-matches one in `shared/`.

ESLint config already exists at `eslint.config.mjs` (created by F-03). We extend it.

## Work

### A. `max-lines` (built-in)
Add to `eslint.config.mjs`:
```js
{
  files: ["desktop/src/**/*.{ts,tsx}", "server/src/**/*.ts", "shared/src/**/*.ts"],
  rules: {
    "max-lines": ["error", { max: 300, skipBlankLines: true, skipComments: true }],
  },
}
```
- Exclude generated files, migrations, and test fixtures
- Verify all current files pass after `calmly-3py.7` (Triage split) lands
- For files that legitimately need to be longer (lock files, etc.), use targeted overrides — not a blanket relaxation

### B. Banned literal enum strings
A custom rule (or use `@typescript-eslint/no-restricted-syntax`) that flags:
- String literals matching the value of any union exported from `@calmly/shared` (e.g. `"open" | "in_progress" | "done"` for `TaskStatus`)
- Suggestion: import the type and use `TaskStatus.OPEN` (or whatever pattern the codebase settles on after `calmly-3py.6` lands)

If a custom rule is too much yak-shaving, settle for a simpler heuristic: ban the specific literals that recur — `"open"`, `"in_progress"`, `"done"`, `"dropped"`, `"telegram"`, `"desktop"` (as bare strings, in non-shared files). Add an override allow-list for migrations and tests.

### C. Forbid wildcard `as` casts in renderer
`@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-assertions` set to `assertionStyle: "as"` and `objectLiteralTypeAssertions: "never"`. Audit caught `as number` casts in `Plan.tsx:156-162` papering over a filter-narrowing failure (see `calmly-3py.21`).

### D. `no-duplicate-imports` + `import/no-duplicates` (already covered — verify)

### E. CI integration
- `pnpm lint` must run on every PR (already in `.github/workflows/`?)
- Husky pre-commit hook runs `lint-staged` → eslint on changed TS files (depends on `calmly-99i` F-03c landing)

## Files
- `eslint.config.mjs`
- new (if custom rule): `tools/eslint-rules/no-shared-enum-literals.cjs`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — add lint job if missing
- `package.json` — `lint-staged` config

## Coordination
- Land **after** `calmly-3py.7` (Triage split) so max-lines doesn't fail on the existing 880-LOC file
- Land **after** `calmly-3py.6` (api-types dedup) so the enum-literal ban doesn't false-positive on legacy code
- Coordinate with `calmly-99i` (F-03c Husky) — pre-commit hook is the delivery mechanism

## Acceptance
- Running `pnpm lint` on a fresh checkout: clean
- Manually adding a 350-LOC component: lint fails
- Manually writing `status: "open"` in renderer code: lint fails with "use TaskStatus from @calmly/shared"
- CI job blocks merge on lint failures

## Severity rationale
P1 — high-leverage gate that catches a whole class of audit findings at commit time, but not strictly blocking the relaunch. Filed under audit-2026-04-30.
close_reason: Prevention work complete; per-file max-lines overrides cite calmly-3py.6/.7 and remove themselves with the audit bead fixes.

title: PREVENT-3: Schema-parity CI test — shared/server/desktop migrations must agree
description:
## Why
**Two of the 4 P0 bugs in `calmly-3py` were schema drift:**
- `calmly-3py.1`: `user_settings` table on server had no `id` column but `shared/src/model/settings.ts` and `apply.ts` required one
- `calmly-3py.4`: `shared/src/model/user.ts` declared `magic_link_token_hash` columns that the server `users` table doesn't have

Both bugs are silent because TypeScript can't see across the SQL boundary. A small CI test could have caught both on the commit that introduced them.

## Work

Build `tools/schema-parity/check.ts`:

1. **Parse the desktop migrations** (`desktop/src/main/db/migrations/*.sql`) — extract each `CREATE TABLE` and `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN`. Build a map: `tableName → { columnName → sqlType }`.
2. **Parse the server migrations** (`server/migrations/*.cjs`) — same. Server uses `node-pg-migrate` so the migrations are JS; either parse the `pgm.createTable` calls (cleanest) or run them against a throwaway Postgres and `\d table` (heavier but exact).
3. **Read the shared zod schemas** (`shared/src/model/*.ts`) — extract the column shape from each `XSchema = z.object({...})`. Use `ts-morph` or a simple regex-based scrape if the schemas are uniform enough.
4. **Compare**: for each table in any of the three sources, assert columns and (loose) types match across all three. Report drift with concrete file:line refs.

### Allow-list for legitimate divergence
Some columns intentionally exist in only one place:
- `users.password_hash` — server-only (auth state shouldn't replicate; once `calmly-3py.4` lands, magic-link columns will be similarly server-only)
- `users.last_seen_at` — desktop-only (local presence)

Express the allow-list as a config file: `tools/schema-parity/allow-list.json`. Each entry needs a comment explaining *why* the divergence is intentional.

## CI integration
- New script: `pnpm schema:check`
- New CI job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` running on every PR that touches `**/migrations/**` or `shared/src/model/**`
- Job fails if drift is detected; PR cannot merge

## Files
- new: `tools/schema-parity/check.ts`
- new: `tools/schema-parity/allow-list.json`
- new: `tools/schema-parity/__tests__/check.test.ts`
- edit: `package.json` — `"schema:check": "tsx tools/schema-parity/check.ts"`
- edit: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — new job

## Acceptance
- Running `pnpm schema:check` on the repo at HEAD passes (after `calmly-3py.1` and `.4` close)
- Manually removing the `id` column from a shared schema: `pnpm schema:check` fails with the offending column + table named
- Manually adding a column to a server migration without updating shared: same failure
- Allow-list explicitly accepts the documented divergences
- CI blocks PRs on failure

## Coordination
- Land **after** `calmly-3py.1` and `calmly-3py.4` close — otherwise CI is red on day one
- Coordinate with `calmly-3py.18` (sync trio in shared schemas) — the parity check should understand that the trio is universal

## Severity rationale
P1 — would have caught 2 of the 4 P0 bugs in this audit alone. Pays for itself the first time it triggers. Filed under audit-2026-04-30.
close_reason: Prevention work complete; calmly-3py.1/.4 drift is in allow-list with TODO comments to remove when audit fixes land.

title: PREVENT-4: E2E suite runs on every PR (not just nightly)
description:
## Why
`calmly-3py.3` (BUG-AUDIT-3) is the textbook case: the worker who built the new Plan view (`c3c7b10`) changed the H1 heading semantics, and `desktop/e2e/foundations/nav.spec.ts:26` started failing — but no one noticed because the e2e suite doesn't run on PRs. The bug landed in main and sat there.

Running e2e on every PR catches this class of regression on the commit that introduces it.

## Why it isn't already done (probably)
- Electron e2e via Playwright is slow (~2-5 min per run)
- Testcontainers Postgres adds another ~30s of warmup
- Workers run frequently → CI minutes add up
The audit found 17 ralph-backup-loop branches in just the last day — if every loop iteration triggered a PR e2e run, the cost compounds.

## Work
1. **Add an e2e job to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`** that runs on:
   - Every PR (open, sync, ready_for_review)
   - Push to `main`
   - Push to `ralph/opus`, `ralph/sonnet` — *unless* the cost is too high; in that case, only run on PRs targeting main
2. **Job scope**: full Playwright suite under `desktop/e2e/foundations/`
3. **Boot ordering**: testcontainers Postgres → server → electron app → run specs
4. **Failure surfaces**:
   - Playwright trace + screenshot uploaded as workflow artifact
   - PR comment posting which spec failed (use `dorny/test-reporter` or similar)
5. **Caching**: aggressive node_modules cache + electron binary cache; aim for warm-cache run < 4 min

## Optimization options if too slow
- Run only the specs whose files (or their imported sources) changed in the diff (use `playwright --grep` or a manual mapping)
- Sharded run across 2-3 GitHub Actions workers
- Skip e2e on docs-only or `.beads/`-only PRs (path filter)

## Coordination
- **Blocked by `calmly-3py.3`** (nav.spec fix) — currently the suite is red, so turning on PR enforcement immediately would block all merges
- Coordinate with `calmly-3py.12` (new e2e specs for Inbox/Triage/Plan) — those specs land via TEST-AUDIT-3 and immediately become PR-gating

## Files
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (add `e2e` job)
- new (maybe): `.github/workflows/e2e-pr.yml` if separating
- `desktop/playwright.config.ts` — verify CI mode is enabled
- `package.json` — `"test:e2e:ci"` script

## Acceptance
- Open a PR that breaks an existing e2e: PR check fails red, with a link to the failing spec and a screenshot artifact
- Open a PR that doesn't touch desktop code: e2e job is skipped or runs in < 30s
- Warm-cache full run completes in < 5 min
- ralph-backup-loop branches don't trigger PR e2e (only PRs targeting main do)

## Severity rationale
P1 — would have caught the nav.spec.ts regression on the commit that introduced it. The audit found this regression days after it landed. Filed under audit-2026-04-30.
close_reason: Prevention work complete; e2e was already on every PR — added docs/beads-only path filter. calmly-3py.3 fix is independent and tracked separately.

title: PREVENT-5: Migrations-touch-shared CODEOWNERS-style check
description:
## Why
Schema drift root cause from `calmly-3py.1` and `calmly-3py.4`: a worker added a column to a migration without updating the corresponding `shared/src/model/<x>.ts`. The `PREVENT-3` schema-parity check catches this *if* the check runs and *if* the change is detectable from SQL parsing, but a simpler upstream gate is: **any PR that touches `**/migrations/**` must also touch `shared/src/model/`**.

This is a path-based check, fast, and doesn't require schema-aware tooling.

## Work
1. Use the GitHub Action `dorny/paths-filter` (or equivalent) to detect paths in the PR diff
2. Add a CI job that:
   - If `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/**` OR `server/migrations/**` is in the diff
   - AND `shared/src/model/**` is NOT in the diff
   - → fail the job with a message linking to PREVENT-3 and PREVENT-1 prompt rules
3. Allow-list: `0001_init.*` files (they're stubs by design — see `calmly-3py.20` checklist)
4. Allow-list: PRs labeled `migrations-only-on-purpose` (escape hatch with audit trail)

## Tradeoffs
- Adds friction for legitimate migrations-only changes (e.g. backfills, index adds). The `migrations-only-on-purpose` label is the escape hatch — but reviewers must check the label is used appropriately.
- Doesn't catch the inverse (shared updated, migration forgotten) — that's PREVENT-3's job. Both gates together are robust.

## Files
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (or new `.github/workflows/path-gates.yml`)

## Acceptance
- A PR adding a column to `server/migrations/0008_*.cjs` without touching `shared/src/model/` fails
- Same PR with `shared/src/model/<x>.ts` updated: passes
- A PR with the `migrations-only-on-purpose` label: passes regardless
- A PR adding only an index (no column changes) still fails by default — use the label for these

## Coordination
- Lower priority than PREVENT-3 (which catches more) but cheaper to build. Land first if PREVENT-3 takes longer.

## Severity rationale
P2 — cheap belt-and-suspenders to PREVENT-3. Filed under audit-2026-04-30.
close_reason: Closed

title: PREVENT-6: Codegen migrations from shared zod schemas (research/explore)
description:
## Why
Even with PREVENT-3 (parity check) and PREVENT-5 (path gate), schema drift between `shared/`, `server/migrations/`, and `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/` is *possible* — the gates only detect it after the diff exists. The architectural answer: **make drift impossible** by code-generating migrations from a single source of truth.

This is research/explore-tier work. The output is a recommendation + spike, not a finished implementation. We may decide the cost isn't worth it.

## Approach (one of three)

### Option A: Drizzle ORM as source of truth
- Define schemas in `shared/src/db/schema.ts` using Drizzle
- Generate Postgres + SQLite migrations via `drizzle-kit`
- Replace `shared/src/model/*.ts` zod schemas with Drizzle's zod adapter (`drizzle-zod`)
- **Pros**: official tooling, dual-dialect supported, active maintenance, type-safe queries on top
- **Cons**: large dependency, learning curve, need to migrate existing migrations

### Option B: Kysely + custom codegen
- Define schemas in TS-native types
- Hand-roll a small codegen that emits both Postgres and SQLite DDL
- **Pros**: less framework lock-in
- **Cons**: write + maintain the codegen ourselves; SQLite/Postgres divergence is finicky

### Option C: Status quo + tooling
- Keep zod schemas as source of truth
- Build a small "schema → migration suggestion" tool that emits a draft migration when a shared schema changes
- Workers manually accept + commit
- **Pros**: minimal disruption
- **Cons**: still possible to bypass; doesn't solve dual-dialect drift

## Work (this is an explore — output is a doc, not code)
1. Spike each option for ~2 hours: prototype changing one column end-to-end
2. Write `docs/schema-codegen-spike.md` covering:
   - Option-by-option findings
   - Cost (engineering hours to migrate, ongoing maintenance)
   - Benefits (concrete: which audit findings would become impossible)
   - Risks (lock-in, dialect quirks for SQLite vs Postgres, our use of FTS5 etc.)
   - Recommendation
3. File a follow-up bd issue if the recommendation is "do it"

## Acceptance
- `docs/schema-codegen-spike.md` exists with the analysis
- A clear recommendation: adopt option X / status-quo
- If "adopt", a follow-up bd issue is filed at appropriate priority with concrete migration steps

## Coordination
- Don't start until `calmly-3py.18` (sync trio in shared) and PREVENT-3 land — they shape the constraints
- This is fine to do during a quieter period of the project

## Severity rationale
P3 — high upside but high cost; a spike to inform the decision, not a commitment. Filed under audit-2026-04-30.
close_reason: Closed

title: PREVENT-7: Schedule recurring audit agent (every 50 commits or 2 weeks)
description:
## Why
This audit (calmly-3py) caught compound debt only because someone ran it. The drift had been compounding for ~12 commits — a few more weeks of unchecked autonomous work and the cleanup cost grows non-linearly.

Make the audit a *routine*, not an event.

## Approach
Use Claude Code's `/schedule` (cloud-side cron) to run an agent that:
1. Pulls latest `main`
2. Runs the same three-pronged audit (desktop main, renderer + e2e, server + shared) using parallel sub-agents — same prompts as the 2026-04-30 audit
3. Cross-references findings against open `audit-*` labeled bd issues (don't refile what's already known)
4. Files new findings as children of a fresh epic: `REFACTOR-EPIC: Audit YYYY-MM-DD`
5. Posts a summary comment on the human's most-recent open PR (or opens a tracking issue) listing severity counts

## Cadence options
- **Time-based**: every 2 weeks (Sunday 22:00 UTC, low worker activity)
- **Commit-count-based**: harder to express in cron, but a daily check that triggers if `git log --since=last-audit | wc -l > 50`
- **Hybrid**: every Sunday, run only if > 30 commits since last audit. The prevention agent itself decides whether to skip.

Recommend **hybrid** — minimizes noise, adapts to project velocity.

## Work
1. Author the audit prompt as a reusable skill or saved agent definition (see `claude-code-guide` for skill setup)
2. The prompt is essentially the three Agent calls from 2026-04-30 — codify them as a single "calmly-audit" skill that:
   - Spawns the three sub-agents in parallel
   - Synthesizes findings into a single epic + children
   - Uses `bd create` (with `--silent`) to file
3. Set up the cron via `/schedule` in Claude Code:
   ```
   /schedule create
     name: calmly-audit
     cron: 0 22 * * 0    # Sunday 22:00 UTC
     prompt: <the audit prompt>
     condition: only run if git rev-list --count <last-audit-tag>..HEAD > 30
   ```
4. After each run, the agent should:
   - Tag main with `audit-YYYY-MM-DD` for next-run cursor
   - Push the bd issues
   - Send a notification (Push notification or PR comment)

## Files
- new: `.claude/skills/calmly-audit.md` (or similar — reusable audit skill)
- new: `docs/recurring-audit.md` — operations doc explaining what the routine does, how to disable, how to interpret findings
- the actual schedule lives in Claude Code config, not in the repo

## Acceptance
- The schedule exists and shows up in `/schedule list`
- A manual trigger (`/schedule run calmly-audit`) successfully:
  - Spawns the three audits
  - Files an epic with children
  - Tags `main`
  - Notifies the human
- Disabling the schedule is documented (e.g. `/schedule pause calmly-audit` or via the web UI)

## Coordination
- Author the audit prompt as a skill **before** scheduling — let the human dry-run it first to verify quality
- The cost: each run is ~3 parallel agent calls, ~100k tokens each = ~300k tokens / 2 weeks. Modest.

## Severity rationale
P1 — without this, the next compounding-debt cycle catches us by surprise. With it, debt is bounded by the audit interval. Filed under audit-2026-04-30.
close_reason: Closed

title: Ralph loop restart: PR-mode merge + ralph_loop.sh:716 bug fix
description: Switch merge-loop.sh from auto-ff-to-main to PR mode (rebase + force-with-lease push to origin/<branch>) so autonomous work lands as branches the user reviews. Use git rebase --autostash to fix the dirty-worktree abort issue. Patch ~/.ralph/ralph_loop.sh:716 arithmetic bug where 'grep -c | echo 0' produced '0\n0' and crashed both workers.

title: F-03b: Playwright Electron config + smoke E2E + CI e2e job
description:
## Goal
Wire Playwright + Electron launcher fixture and a single smoke E2E that boots the app and asserts the SignIn screen renders (default unauthenticated state). Extend CI with a Linux-only e2e job.

## Skills
Invoke playwright-electron-debugger before starting. Electron + Playwright has flake patterns (sandbox flags on Linux CI, hot-reload races on dev URL, ABI mismatch when better-sqlite3 isn't rebuilt) that the skill addresses directly.

## Scope
- desktop/playwright.config.ts — projectName "electron", testDir desktop/e2e/.
- desktop/e2e/fixtures/electronApp.ts — _electron.launch fixture using the prod build (not dev server) so the test is hermetic.
- desktop/e2e/smoke.spec.ts — launch app, wait for window, assert SignIn renders ("Welcome to Calmly.").
- Add scripts: pnpm --filter @calmly/desktop test:e2e.
- Extend .github/workflows/ci.yml with an "e2e" job (Linux runner, depends on build job, runs the playwright tests; uploads trace artifact on failure).

## Acceptance
- pnpm --filter @calmly/desktop test:e2e passes locally on Linux (best-effort on Windows).
- CI e2e job passes on the Linux runner.
- A failed E2E run uploads a Playwright trace via actions/upload-artifact.

## Depends on
- F-03a (calmly-fw2): the CI workflow scaffold and pnpm lint pipeline.
notes:
LANDED. Built playwright.config.ts + e2e/fixtures/electronApp.ts + e2e/smoke.spec.ts; added test:e2e script + @playwright/test devDep; extended .github/workflows/ci.yml with Linux-only e2e job (xvfb-run, libnss3 et al, --no-sandbox flag, trace artifact upload on failure); wired e2e dir into tsconfig.node.json + ESLint config + .gitignore.

Bonus: smoke test caught two pre-existing prod-build crashers introduced by F-13b/F-02:
1. desktop/src/main/logging/electron-log-transport.ts — changed 'electron-log/main' → 'electron-log/main.js'. electron-log v5 has no exports field, so Node ESM rejects extensionless subpath imports at packaged-app boot.
2. desktop/electron.vite.config.ts + src/main/index.ts — preload was emitting ESM (.mjs), but sandbox:true preloads must be CommonJS. Forced format:['cjs'] + fileName 'index.cjs' in vite config; updated webPreferences.preload path to match. Without this, contextBridge never installed and the renderer crashed on window.calmly.auth access.

These were untested in prior PRs because vitest runs only on src/ and no one had launched the prod electron build. The smoke test now guards both regressions.

Acceptance: pnpm --filter @calmly/desktop test:e2e passes locally on Windows in ~6s; CI job has trace artifact upload on failure. Ready to close.
close_reason: Closed

title: Telegram bot: linking, capture, voice, commands, outbound
description:
## Goal
Ship the Telegram bot mobile surface: account linking via one-time code, inbound text/voice → Inbox, voice transcription via cloud API, basic slash commands (/now, /today, /inbox), and outbound message infrastructure for reminders to layer on top of in Epic 4.

## Build order
PRD §23 step 3 (Telegram bot).

## Scope
- Telegram bot app (webhook server) with health check
- /start `<linking-code>` flow: generate one-time code in desktop app → user pastes in bot → server links chat ID to user
- Inbound text message → InboxItem (source = telegram-text)
- Inbound voice note → cloud transcription (Whisper or provider equivalent) → InboxItem (source = telegram-voice); raw audio retained until transcription succeeds, then discarded
- /now: show current focus task + next step
- /today: show today's plan
- /inbox: show inbox count + first few items
- Outbound message infra: send Telegram messages with inline action buttons (foundation for Epic 4)
- Settings → Telegram page: linking UI, status, unlink

## Out of scope
- Reminder scheduling/dispatching (Epic 4)
- Reminder action handlers like Done/Snooze/Reschedule (Epic 4)

## Done when
A user with a Telegram account can link in Settings, send a text or voice note that lands in Inbox, and run /now /today /inbox successfully.

## References
PRD §7 mobile surface, §11 Capture (Telegram), §17 Cloud transcription, §22 Risks (Telegram skew).

title: TG-01: Telegram bot service skeleton (webhook + health + env)
description:
## Goal
Stand up the Telegram bot service skeleton inside the existing Fastify sync server: webhook endpoint, bot client wrapper, env config for `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, and a health probe that confirms `getMe` succeeds. This unblocks every other Telegram task.

## Scope
- New module at `server/src/telegram/` with: `bot.ts` (bot client wrapper), `webhook.ts` (Fastify route), `config.ts` (env validation), `index.ts` (registers plugin)
- Use `grammy` (or `node-telegram-bot-api`) — pick `grammy` for typed updates; document choice in `bot.ts` header
- Webhook route: `POST /telegram/webhook` — verifies Telegram secret-token header (`X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token`), delegates to update dispatcher
- `GET /telegram/health` returns `{ ok, botUsername, webhookSet }` — calls `getMe` and `getWebhookInfo`
- Environment vars (added to `server/.env.example`): `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_URL` (public URL for `setWebhook`)
- CLI helper script `server/scripts/telegram-set-webhook.ts` that calls `setWebhook` with the configured URL + secret
- Update dispatcher stub: receives Update, logs `update_id` + type, returns 200 immediately. Real handlers are added in tg03/tg05/tg06.
- Pino redaction for `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`

## Files
- `server/src/telegram/bot.ts`
- `server/src/telegram/webhook.ts`
- `server/src/telegram/config.ts`
- `server/src/telegram/dispatcher.ts`
- `server/src/telegram/index.ts`
- `server/scripts/telegram-set-webhook.ts`
- `server/.env.example` (append vars)
- `server/src/app.ts` (register plugin if not already wired)

## Acceptance
- `pnpm --filter @calmly/server dev` starts and `GET /telegram/health` returns `botUsername` matching the configured bot
- Posting a fake Update JSON to `/telegram/webhook` with the wrong secret returns 401; with the correct secret returns 200 and logs `update_id`
- Boot fails fast with a clear message if `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` is missing
- `pnpm --filter @calmly/server typecheck` passes
- `telegram-set-webhook.ts` run against a test bot successfully registers the webhook (manually verified)

## Notes
- No DB writes in this task — dispatcher is a pure stub.
- Linking, capture, and slash commands are deliberately out of scope; they layer on top via the dispatcher.
- Use long polling locally only for manual debugging; production path is webhook.

## References
PRD §7 Mobile surface — Telegram bot, §20 Architecture (webhook), §23 step 3.

title: TG-02: Linking flow (one-time code + /start handler + TelegramLink)
description:
## Goal
Implement account linking between desktop and Telegram via a one-time code: desktop generates code → user runs `/start <code>` in bot → server links `chat_id` ↔ `user_id` and persists a `TelegramLink` row.

## Scope
- Server endpoint `POST /telegram/linking/code` (auth required) — creates a `telegram_linking_code` row: 8-char alphanumeric, expires in 15 min, single-use, scoped to a user
- Server endpoint `GET /telegram/linking/status` — returns `{ linked: bool, chatId?, telegramUsername?, linkedAt? }`
- Server endpoint `POST /telegram/linking/unlink` — deletes the `TelegramLink` row
- Bot handler for `/start <code>`:
  - if no code: reply with onboarding text directing to desktop Settings → Telegram
  - if code valid + unused + not expired: create `TelegramLink` row, mark code consumed, reply with success
  - if invalid/expired/used: friendly error message
- Migration: `telegram_links` table (`user_id`, `chat_id` unique, `telegram_username`, `linked_at`) and `telegram_linking_codes` table (`code` unique, `user_id`, `expires_at`, `consumed_at` nullable)
- Rate-limit code generation: max 5 active codes per user
- Audit log entry on link/unlink

## Files
- `server/migrations/00xx_telegram_links.sql`
- `server/src/telegram/linking.ts` (route handlers + service)
- `server/src/telegram/handlers/start.ts` (bot handler)
- `server/src/telegram/dispatcher.ts` (route `/start` to handler)
- `server/src/telegram/index.ts` (register linking routes)
- `shared/src/types/telegram.ts` (TelegramLink, LinkingCode types — Zod)

## Acceptance
- Authenticated `POST /telegram/linking/code` returns a fresh code; calling again creates an additional code (capped at 5)
- Sending `/start <validCode>` to the bot creates a `telegram_links` row and replies with success message
- Re-sending the same code returns "code already used"; expired codes return expired error
- `GET /telegram/linking/status` reflects linked state correctly before and after unlink
- A user can only have one active link; re-linking from a different chat replaces the previous link and logs the change
- Integration test simulates the full flow with a mocked bot client

## Notes
- The desktop UI is built in tg08; this task only ships server endpoints + bot handler.
- Codes are case-insensitive on input; stored uppercase.
- Store `chat_id` as `BIGINT` — Telegram chat IDs exceed 32-bit.

## References
PRD §7 Telegram bot (Linking), §14 Data Model (TelegramLink), §23 step 3.

title: TG-03: Inbound text -> InboxItem (source=telegram-text)
description:
## Goal
When a linked Telegram user sends a plain text message to the bot (not a slash command), create an `InboxItem` with `source = 'telegram-text'` belonging to that user, and confirm receipt.

## Scope
- Bot text-message handler: filters out commands (anything starting with `/`)
- Resolve user from `chat_id` via `telegram_links`; if unlinked, reply with prompt to link via desktop Settings
- Create `InboxItem`:
  - `user_id` from link
  - `source = 'telegram-text'`
  - `raw_text` from message
  - `created_at = now()`
  - `external_ref = 'tg:<chat_id>:<message_id>'` for idempotency
- Idempotency: if `external_ref` already exists, do not duplicate; reply with original confirmation
- Reply with a short ack (e.g., "Saved to inbox.") — keep it terse per ADHD principle
- Long messages (> 4000 chars) are truncated and noted in the ack
- Telemetry counter: `telegram_capture_text` (only if telemetry opt-in flag is set)

## Files
- `server/src/telegram/handlers/text.ts`
- `server/src/telegram/dispatcher.ts` (wire text handler)
- `server/src/inbox/service.ts` (add `createFromTelegram` method, or extend existing create)
- Tests: `server/src/telegram/handlers/text.test.ts`

## Acceptance
- Linked user sending "buy milk" creates one `InboxItem` row with `source='telegram-text'` and gets ack reply
- Re-sending the same `message_id` (simulated via Update replay) does NOT create a duplicate
- Unlinked chat_id receives the link-prompt reply; no inbox row created
- Slash commands are NOT treated as text capture (they pass through to slash-command handlers in tg05/tg06)
- Test coverage: linked happy path, unlinked, idempotency, truncation

## Notes
- Editing a Telegram message (`edited_message`) is out of scope; only `message` updates capture.
- Photos/files/stickers — out of scope; reply with "I only handle text and voice notes for now."
- Voice handled in tg04.

## References
PRD §11 Capture (Telegram), §14 InboxItem, §7 Telegram capture.

title: TG-04: Inbound voice -> cloud transcription -> InboxItem
description:
## Goal
Handle inbound Telegram voice notes: download the audio, transcribe via cloud API (Whisper / equivalent), create an `InboxItem` with `source='telegram-voice'` containing the transcript, and discard the raw audio after success.

## Scope
- Voice-message handler in dispatcher: triggers on `message.voice` updates
- Audio download via Telegram `getFile` API → temp path under `server/tmp/telegram-voice/<update_id>.ogg`
- Transcription adapter `server/src/transcription/`:
  - Interface `TranscriptionProvider { transcribe(buffer, mimeType): Promise<{ text, durationSec }> }`
  - `OpenAIWhisperProvider` (POST to `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, model `whisper-1`)
  - `MockProvider` for tests
  - Provider selected via `TRANSCRIPTION_PROVIDER` env (default `openai`)
- Server-side API key for transcription (`OPENAI_TRANSCRIPTION_KEY`) — separate from per-user keys; this is one MVP-acceptable place where the server holds a key
- On success: create `InboxItem` with `source='telegram-voice'`, `raw_text=transcript`, `meta={duration_sec, original_message_id}`; delete the temp audio file
- On failure: reply with friendly error per PRD §13; retain audio in temp for up to 1 hour for one retry, then purge
- Reply ack: "Saved to inbox: <first 80 chars of transcript>…"
- Max audio duration: 5 min — longer voices reply with "Voice note too long; please shorten."

## Files
- `server/src/telegram/handlers/voice.ts`
- `server/src/transcription/index.ts`
- `server/src/transcription/openai.ts`
- `server/src/transcription/mock.ts`
- `server/src/transcription/types.ts`
- `server/.env.example` (append `OPENAI_TRANSCRIPTION_KEY`, `TRANSCRIPTION_PROVIDER`)
- Tests: `server/src/telegram/handlers/voice.test.ts` (uses MockProvider)

## Acceptance
- Voice message ≤ 5 min from a linked user produces an `InboxItem` with non-empty `raw_text` and the temp audio file is deleted
- Transcription failure produces an error reply matching PRD §13 wording; no `InboxItem` created; audio retained for 1h for retry
- Voice > 5 min replies with the length error and is not transcribed
- Unit tests with `MockProvider` cover happy path, provider error, file-too-large
- Pino logs do not include the transcript content (PII) at info level

## Notes
- Telegram voice notes are OGG/Opus; do NOT transcode unless provider rejects (Whisper accepts OGG).
- Per PRD §17: cloud transcription only; no local STT in MVP.
- `OPENAI_TRANSCRIPTION_KEY` is a project-owned key for MVP simplicity. Per-user-key transcription is out of scope.
- Depends on tg01 (bot skeleton), tg02 (linking), tg03 (InboxItem creation pattern).

## References
PRD §11 Capture (voice), §17 Cloud transcription, §13 Error states (voice transcription failed), §22 Risks.

title: TG-06: /today and /inbox slash commands
description:
## Goal

title: TG-07: Outbound message infra (action buttons + callback router)
description:
## Goal
Build the outbound message infrastructure: a primitive that sends a Telegram message with inline action buttons and persists `OutboundMessage` records so action callbacks can be routed back to the originating intent. This is the foundation Epic 4 (reminders) layers on top of.

## Scope
- `server/src/telegram/outbound.ts` exposing:
  - `sendMessage(userId, { text, buttons })` — `buttons` is `[{ label, actionId, payload }]`
  - Resolves `chat_id` from `telegram_links`; throws `TelegramNotLinkedError` if no link
  - Builds `inline_keyboard` with `callback_data = "<actionId>:<msgId>"` (Telegram callback_data is 64 bytes — encode minimally; full payload stored in DB)
  - Persists `OutboundMessage` row before sending (id, user_id, chat_id, intent, payload JSON, sent_at, telegram_message_id, status)
- Migration: `outbound_messages` table
- Callback handler in dispatcher: receives `callback_query` updates, parses `<actionId>:<msgId>`, looks up `OutboundMessage`, dispatches to action handler registry, calls `answerCallbackQuery`
- Action handler registry: `registerAction(actionId, handler)` — Epic 4 plugs Done/Snooze/Reschedule into this
- Retry logic: on Telegram 5xx or network error, retry 3x with exponential backoff; on 403 (user blocked bot), mark `status='blocked'` and emit a domain event so reminders engine can fall back to desktop notifications
- Edit message support: `editMessage(outboundMessageId, { text, buttons })` for snooze acknowledgements

## Files
- `server/migrations/00xx_outbound_messages.sql`
- `server/src/telegram/outbound.ts`
- `server/src/telegram/actions.ts` (registry)
- `server/src/telegram/handlers/callback.ts`
- `server/src/telegram/dispatcher.ts` (wire callback_query)
- `shared/src/types/telegram.ts` (OutboundMessage type)
- Tests: `server/src/telegram/outbound.test.ts`, `callback.test.ts`

## Acceptance
- `sendMessage` to a linked user creates an `outbound_messages` row and the user receives the message with the configured buttons
- `sendMessage` to an unlinked user throws `TelegramNotLinkedError`; no row created
- Pressing a button triggers the registered action handler with the resolved payload
- Telegram 403 marks the row `status='blocked'` and emits the domain event (verified via test spy)
- `editMessage` updates the existing message in place (no new row)
- Retries: simulated 5xx is retried 3x then surfaces a clear error

## Notes
- Action handlers themselves (Done/Snooze/Reschedule) are in Epic 4 (rm04, rm06). This task only ships the substrate.
- `callback_data` is intentionally short — the full payload belongs in `outbound_messages.payload`.
- Domain event for `blocked` status is consumed by Epic 4's dispatcher fallback (rm05).

## References
PRD §11 Reminders (delivery + actions), §7 Telegram bot, §13 Error states (Telegram offline/blocked).

title: TG-09: Telegram bot integration test pass (mocked Telegram + voice)
description:
## Goal
Integration test pass for the Telegram bot mobile surface: linking flow, inbound text/voice → InboxItem, slash commands, outbound action-button messages. Mocks the Telegram Bot API and the cloud transcription provider so tests run hermetically.

  1. **Linking**: desktop generates code → bot receives `/start <code>` → DB shows `telegram_links` row with chat_id ↔ user_id
  2. **Inbound text**: webhook `update` with text → InboxItem row created with `source='telegram-text'` and matching raw_text

title: AI v1: BYO-key cloud (Anthropic) - triage cleanup, Make Startable, brain-dump split
description:
## Goal
Ship the first AI surface: cloud-only via single provider (Anthropic) with BYO API key. Three actions: triage cleanup, "Make Startable" task breakdown, brain-dump splitting. All actions are user-invoked, transparent, and undoable.

## Build order
PRD §23 step 7 (AI v1, cloud-only, single provider).

## Scope
- Settings → AI page (initial): enable toggle, mode (Off/Cloud only), provider=Anthropic, BYO key entry stored encrypted
- AI orchestration layer: prompt templates, request/response, error handling, token accounting
- Triage cleanup action (suggest type/title/date/next-action) on Inbox/Triage UI
- Make Startable action on a task: AI breaks vague task into clearer next-action(s)
- Brain-dump split action: splits a paste/long item into multiple inbox items
- Suggestion review UI: accept / edit / reject; AISuggestion record persisted with outcome
- Fallback behavior: API key missing/invalid/quota/timeout → inline message + fix path; never block deterministic flow

## Out of scope (deferred to Epic 8)
- Ollama / local mode
- Second provider (OpenAI)
- Hybrid routing
- Stuck rescue, daily planning, replan suggestions

## Done when
With an Anthropic key entered, all three AI actions work end-to-end with editable suggestions and graceful failure when the key/network/quota is bad.

## References
PRD §6 AI Posture, §7 desktop item 11, §16 AI Settings, §17 AI Technical Posture (cloud), §22 Key Risks (latency, hallucination).

title: AI1-01: Settings → AI page v1 (toggle, mode=Cloud only, Anthropic BYO key)
description:
## Goal
Build the Settings → AI page (v1 subset): an enable toggle, mode selector locked to Off/Cloud only, provider locked to Anthropic, and a BYO API key entry that writes through the F-12 secret store. This is the user-facing entry point that gates every AI feature in Epic 7.

title: AI1-02: AI orchestration layer (provider interface, Anthropic impl, prompts, error categorization)
description:
## Goal
Build the AI orchestration layer in `desktop/src/main/ai/`: a provider-agnostic interface, the Anthropic concrete implementation, prompt templates for the three v1 actions, request/response shapes, and categorized error handling. This is the spine every Epic 7 action calls into.

## Scope
- Provider interface:
  ```ts
  interface AIProvider {
    name: 'anthropic' | 'openai' | 'ollama'
    complete(req: AIRequest): Promise<AIResponse>
  }
  ```
- `AIRequest` carries `promptClass` (`'triage_cleanup' | 'make_startable' | 'brain_dump_split'`), structured input, max tokens, timeout
- `AIResponse` carries structured output (zod-validated), token counts, model id, latency ms
- Anthropic implementation: `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, fetches key from secret store on each call, never caches key in renderer-reachable memory
- Prompt templates module with one template per `promptClass` and a single shared system preamble (anti-hallucination rules: be concrete, no invented dates, accept-edit-reject framing)
- Error categorization → typed union:
  - `AIError = { kind: 'auth' } | { kind: 'quota' } | { kind: 'network' } | { kind: 'timeout' } | { kind: 'invalid_response' } | { kind: 'unknown', cause }`
- Single dispatch function `runAI(promptClass, input)` that selects provider (v1: hard-coded Anthropic if mode=Cloud) and returns `Result<AIResponse, AIError>`
- All structured outputs validated with Zod; validation failure → `invalid_response`

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/ai/index.ts` — `runAI` dispatcher
- `desktop/src/main/ai/types.ts` — interfaces, Result, AIError
- `desktop/src/main/ai/providers/anthropic.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/ai/prompts/triageCleanup.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/ai/prompts/makeStartable.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/ai/prompts/brainDumpSplit.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/ai/prompts/system.ts` — shared preamble
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/ai.ts` — narrow IPC: `runTriageCleanup`, `runMakeStartable`, `runBrainDumpSplit`
- `desktop/src/preload/ai.ts`
- Unit tests: `desktop/src/main/ai/__tests__/anthropic.test.ts` (with sdk mocked)

## Acceptance
- `runAI('triage_cleanup', {...})` with mocked Anthropic returns a Zod-validated structured suggestion
- Forcing 401 from the mocked SDK yields `AIError { kind: 'auth' }`
- Forcing 429 yields `kind: 'quota'`
- Forcing a 30s hang exceeds timeout and yields `kind: 'timeout'` (configurable, default 20s)
- Forcing malformed JSON yields `kind: 'invalid_response'`
- Renderer cannot import the provider directly; only the IPC channel is reachable

## Notes
- This task does NOT persist suggestions — that's `ai1_suggestion_persistence`.
- This task does NOT render UI — UI tasks consume the IPC.
- Provider interface is generic on purpose so Epic 8's OpenAI + Ollama implementations slot in without refactoring callers.

## References
PRD §6 AI Posture, §17 AI Technical Posture (cloud), §22 Risks (latency, hallucination), §13 (error categories).

title: AI1-03: AISuggestion persistence (record model, prompt class, accept/reject/edit outcome)
description:
## Goal
Persist every AI invocation as an `AISuggestion` row (table from F-05) so we can record source model, prompt class, and accepted/rejected/edited outcome for telemetry and future eval.

## Scope
- Repository module wrapping the `ai_suggestions` table:
  - `recordPending({ ownerType, ownerId?, model, promptClass, suggestionJson }) → suggestionId`
  - `recordOutcome(suggestionId, outcome: 'accepted' | 'rejected' | 'edited', editedJson?)`
- `runAI` dispatcher (from `ai1_orchestration`) writes a `pending` row after a successful response and returns the `suggestionId` alongside the suggestion
- All three action UI tasks call `recordOutcome` when the user clicks accept / reject / edit-then-save
- `ownerId` is nullable for not-yet-attached suggestions (e.g., a brain-dump split before items are created)
- Hooks for opt-in telemetry: surface `accept_rate` per `promptClass` in a debug query (no remote send yet — Epic 9)

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/ai/persistence.ts` — repository
- `desktop/src/main/ai/index.ts` — extend `runAI` to record pending row + return id
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/ai.ts` — extend with `recordSuggestionOutcome`
- `desktop/src/preload/ai.ts` — expose outcome reporter
- Unit test: `desktop/src/main/ai/__tests__/persistence.test.ts`

## Acceptance
- After running any v1 action, exactly one `ai_suggestions` row exists with `outcome='pending'`
- Calling `recordOutcome(id, 'accepted')` flips the row's `outcome` and stores `accepted_at`
- `recordOutcome(id, 'edited', editedJson)` stores the edited payload alongside the original
- Querying `SELECT prompt_class, outcome, COUNT(*) FROM ai_suggestions GROUP BY 1,2` returns expected counts in test

## Notes
- Schema columns already exist from F-05; this task only writes the repo + wiring.
- Do not log full suggestion text to disk logs (PRD §18 telemetry: never capture task content) — DB only.
- Edited payload stores the user's final value, not a diff.

## References
PRD §14 (AISuggestion), §18 Telemetry (accept/reject/edit rates), §21 Success Criteria (≥40% accept rate).

title: AI1-04: Triage cleanup action UI (type/title/date/next-action with accept-edit-reject)
description:
## Goal
Add the Triage cleanup AI action to the Inbox/Triage UI: on a single inbox item the user can invoke AI to suggest type, cleaned-up title, due date, and a clearer next-action — each individually editable, accept-able, or reject-able.

## Scope
- "AI cleanup" button on the Triage card (visible only when AI is enabled and a key is set)
- On click: call `window.calmly.ai.runTriageCleanup({ rawText })` → renders a side-panel with four suggestion fields:
  - `type` (task | event | someday) — chips
  - `title` (cleaned)
  - `dueDate` (parsed, with original-string label)
  - `nextAction` (single-sentence concrete next step)
- Each field has an inline editor and per-field accept/reject; a top-level `Apply all` and `Discard`
- On `Apply all` or per-field accept: writes to the inbox item / created task; on accept, triggers `recordSuggestionOutcome(id, 'accepted' | 'edited')`
- Loading state with spinner + cancel; cancel aborts the in-flight request
- Failure: pass-through to `ai1_inline_failures` UI (do not implement messages here)
- Keyboard: `A` accept all, `R` reject all, `E` focus first editable field

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/inbox/TriageCard.tsx` — add AI button + panel mount point
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/inbox/AICleanupPanel.tsx` — the suggestion editor
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/inbox/AICleanupPanel.module.css`
- `desktop/src/renderer/state/aiTriage.ts` — local state hook
- E2E test: `desktop/e2e/triage-ai-cleanup.spec.ts`

## Acceptance
- With a stubbed `runTriageCleanup` returning a fixed payload, the panel renders all four fields, each editable
- Accepting one field updates only that field on the underlying item; the other three remain untouched
- `Apply all` writes all four fields and closes the panel
- `Discard` closes the panel without mutating the item, and records `outcome='rejected'`
- Cancel during loading aborts the request and does not record any outcome
- AI button is hidden when AI is disabled in Settings

## Notes
- This task only consumes the orchestration IPC; do not call Anthropic SDK directly from the renderer.
- Date parsing is the model's job; the UI just shows what came back. If the date is implausible, the user edits it.
- Inbox/Triage card is the existing Epic 2 component; only extend, do not rewrite.

## References
PRD §11 Triage (AI suggestions), §6 AI Posture (transparent + editable), §22 (hallucination risk → editable suggestions).

title: AI1-05: Make Startable action UI (AI proposes clearer next-action on a task)
description:
## Goal
Add the "Make Startable" AI action on a task: AI proposes a clearer concrete next-action (and optionally up to 2 sub-steps) for a vague task; user can accept, edit, or reject.

## Scope
- "Make Startable" button on the Task detail panel and Focus screen (visible when AI enabled + key present)
- On click: call `window.calmly.ai.runMakeStartable({ taskId, title, notes })` → modal with:
  - Suggested `nextAction` (single sentence)
  - Optional `subSteps[]` (up to 2 short bullets)
  - Per-field edit + accept/reject; bottom `Apply` and `Discard`
- On `Apply`: updates the task's `next_action` field (extend tasks repo if not already present from Epic 2) and optionally creates child tasks for sub-steps using F-05 `parent_task_id`
- Records outcome via `recordSuggestionOutcome` with `ownerType='task', ownerId=taskId`
- Loading state with cancel; failure → delegated to `ai1_inline_failures`

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/task/TaskDetail.tsx` — add button
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/focus/FocusToolbar.tsx` — add button
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/ai/MakeStartableModal.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/ai/MakeStartableModal.module.css`
- `desktop/src/main/repositories/tasks.ts` — extend if `next_action` field write missing
- E2E test: `desktop/e2e/make-startable.spec.ts`

## Acceptance
- With stubbed orchestration, a vague task ("write the thing") yields a concrete next action visible in the modal
- Accept writes `next_action` to the task; sub-steps create child tasks with `parent_task_id` set
- Reject closes the modal without DB writes and records `outcome='rejected'`
- Editing the suggestion before accept records `outcome='edited'`
- Modal is keyboard-navigable (Tab, Enter, Esc)

## Notes
- Sub-steps are capped at 2 to avoid over-decomposition (PRD §11: lightweight, not project management).
- Do not auto-start a focus session on accept — that's a deliberate user action.

## References
PRD §11 Triage (break it down), §11 Focus (one current task + next step), §6 AI uses (Make Startable).

title: AI1-06: Brain-dump split action UI (paste long block → N inbox items, per-item confirm)
description:
## Goal
Add the Brain-dump split AI action: paste a long block of text into Capture; AI proposes N inbox items; user confirms each individually before any are created.

## Scope
- In Capture, when input has more than 200 chars or contains 2+ line breaks, surface a `Split with AI` affordance (in addition to normal `Save as one item`)
- On click: call `window.calmly.ai.runBrainDumpSplit({ text })` → returns `items: { rawText, suggestedTitle, suggestedType }[]`
- Render a confirmation list:
  - Each row: checkbox (default checked), editable title, type chip, raw-text preview (collapsed)
  - `Create N items` (count reflects checked rows) and `Cancel`
- On confirm: insert one `inbox_items` row per checked entry with `source='ai-split'` (matches F-05 enum)
- Records one parent suggestion plus per-item child outcomes (accepted/rejected/edited)
- Loading state + cancel; failure → delegated to `ai1_inline_failures`

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/capture/CaptureBar.tsx` — add `Split with AI` button + threshold logic
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/ai/BrainDumpSplitModal.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/ai/BrainDumpSplitModal.module.css`
- `desktop/src/main/repositories/inboxItems.ts` — extend with `bulkInsert` if missing
- E2E test: `desktop/e2e/brain-dump-split.spec.ts`

## Acceptance
- With stubbed orchestration returning 4 items, the modal lists 4 editable rows
- Unchecking 1 row and confirming creates exactly 3 inbox items
- Each created item has `source='ai-split'`
- Edited title is the value persisted (not the original suggestion)
- Cancel creates zero items and records all-rejected outcome
- The original input is NOT also saved as a single item when split is used

## Notes
- The 200-char / 2-newline threshold is intentionally low so the affordance shows up.
- Keep the modal scrollable; cap render at 20 rows with a "show more" if AI returns more.
- Do not auto-triage the created items — they land in inbox like any capture.

## References
PRD §11 Capture (brain-dump splitting), §6 AI uses (brain-dump splitting), §14 InboxItem source enum.

title: AI1-07: Inline failure UI for all three AI actions (auth/quota/network/timeout/invalid)
description:
## Goal
Provide a single, consistent inline failure UI used by all three v1 AI actions. Each failure category from `ai1_orchestration` (auth / quota / network / timeout / invalid_response) maps to a clear message, a fix path, and never blocks the deterministic flow.

## Scope
- Reusable `<AIFailureBanner>` component consuming `AIError` and rendering:
  - `auth` → "Your Anthropic key was rejected. [Update key in Settings]"
  - `quota` → "Anthropic quota exhausted. [See your usage]"
  - `network` → "Couldn't reach Anthropic. [Retry] [Continue without AI]"
  - `timeout` → "Anthropic took too long. [Retry] [Continue without AI]"
  - `invalid_response` → "AI returned something unusable. [Retry] [Report]"
- Banner appears inside the action's surface (Triage panel, Make Startable modal, Brain-dump modal) — never as a global toast
- `[Retry]` re-issues the same request without losing user input
- `[Update key in Settings]` deep-links to the AI settings page
- Deterministic path is always still reachable: e.g., during Triage failure the user can still classify manually
- Error events feed `ai_suggestions` with `outcome='rejected'` and an `error_kind` annotation in the JSON for telemetry

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/ai/AIFailureBanner.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/ai/AIFailureBanner.module.css`
- `desktop/src/renderer/state/aiErrors.ts` — small hook for retry orchestration
- Wire-ups in: `AICleanupPanel.tsx`, `MakeStartableModal.tsx`, `BrainDumpSplitModal.tsx`
- Unit test: `desktop/src/renderer/components/ai/__tests__/AIFailureBanner.test.tsx`

## Acceptance
- Stubbing each `AIError` kind in turn renders the correct message and action set
- Clicking `Retry` calls the same orchestration function with original args
- Clicking `Update key in Settings` navigates to `/settings/ai`
- During a failure, the underlying inbox item / task / capture text is preserved (no data loss)
- Banner copy matches PRD §13 ("what happened, what they can do, whether anything is lost")

## Notes
- This task is purely UI + wiring; the error categorization itself lives in `ai1_orchestration`.
- Copy must not blame the user (anti-shame principle, PRD §4).
- Future: Epic 8 will reuse this banner for Ollama/OpenAI failure kinds — keep the component generic on `AIError`.

## References
PRD §13 Error states (API key missing/invalid, quota exceeded, call failed/timed out), §6 Failure behavior, §4 anti-shame.
