title: AI1-08: Token accounting + rate-limit handling (estimate, record, throttle, 429 backoff)
description:
## Goal
Track token usage and respect rate limits so the user's BYO Anthropic quota is never silently burned. Show estimated tokens before send for higher-cost actions and aggregate per-day usage in Settings.

## Scope
- Pre-flight estimator: a small token-counting helper (Anthropic's tokenizer or a conservative char/4 fallback) returns `{ inputEstimate, maxOutput }` for any prompt
- Brain-dump split modal shows "~X input tokens" before the user confirms (highest input variability)
- On every `runAI` response, persist `{ ts, promptClass, inputTokens, outputTokens, model }` to a new `ai_usage` table (or extend `ai_suggestions`)
- Settings → AI page surfaces a "Today's usage" panel: total requests, input tokens, output tokens, broken down by `promptClass`
- Soft client-side rate limiter: if more than N requests in M seconds across the app, queue with a small "AI is catching up…" indicator (configurable defaults: 5 req / 10 s)
- Honors Anthropic 429: on `quota` error, suspend further AI calls for 60s with a banner

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/ai/usage.ts` — estimator + recorder + reader
- `desktop/src/main/ai/rateLimiter.ts` — simple token-bucket
- `desktop/src/main/ai/index.ts` — wire usage recorder + rate limiter into `runAI`
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/00XX_ai_usage.sql` — `ai_usage(id, user_id, ts, prompt_class, input_tokens, output_tokens, model)`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/settings/AIUsagePanel.tsx`
- Unit tests: `desktop/src/main/ai/__tests__/rateLimiter.test.ts`, `usage.test.ts`

## Acceptance
- After 3 successful runs, `ai_usage` has 3 rows with non-zero token counts
- Settings panel renders today's totals; restarting the app preserves them
- Bursting 10 calls in 1s causes calls 6-10 to queue (verified by timestamps)
- Quota error suspends new calls for 60s; existing UI shows the banner; deterministic flows remain usable
- Brain-dump modal shows an estimate within ±20% of the actual `input_tokens` recorded post-call

## Notes
- This is the chokepoint that protects user money — keep it simple but always-on.
- Do not bundle a heavyweight tokenizer; the char/4 fallback is acceptable for v1.
- Numbers are local-only; never sent to the sync server (PRD §18: opt-in telemetry, key content never sent).

## References
PRD §17 (BYO key, no server-side proxy), §22 (latency, quota), §13 (quota exceeded), §18 telemetry boundaries.

title: AI1-09: AI v1 integration test (mocked Anthropic, all actions, failures)
description:
## Goal
Integration test pass for AI v1 — mocked Anthropic provider exercising all three actions (triage cleanup, Make Startable, brain-dump split) end-to-end, including suggestion persistence, accept/edit/reject flows, and every documented failure mode.

## Scope
- Mock Anthropic API server (`desktop/test/mocks/anthropic.ts`) returning canned messages tied to prompt class
- A small real-prompt regression suite (cassette-based via `nock`) — runs on demand only, not in CI default, gated by `RUN_REAL_AI_TESTS=1`
- Specs (Vitest + Playwright):
  1. **Triage cleanup happy path**: vague InboxItem "thing about car" → mock returns `{ type: 'task', title: 'Take car for service', due: 'Friday', next_action: 'Call dealership' }` → user accepts → Task row matches
  2. **Triage cleanup edit**: same path, user edits the title before accept → AISuggestion.outcome='edited', title is the edited value
  3. **Triage cleanup reject**: user rejects → InboxItem unchanged, AISuggestion.outcome='rejected'
  4. **Make Startable**: vague task "draft proposal" → mock returns `["open last year's proposal", "list 5 changes", "block 90 min"]` → user accepts → 3 child tasks created with parent_task_id set
  5. **Brain-dump split**: paste 4-line dump → mock returns 4 candidates → user de-selects one → 3 InboxItems created
  6. **Failure: missing key** — settings shows the action button as disabled with tooltip explaining
  7. **Failure: invalid key** — Anthropic mock returns 401 → inline message "Your Anthropic key is invalid. Update in Settings → AI." with a deep-link button
  8. **Failure: quota exceeded** — mock returns 429 → inline message + suggestion to switch off AI temporarily
  9. **Failure: timeout** — mock delays past timeout → inline error + "Try again" button; deterministic flow still works
  10. **Token accounting**: each call increments a counter visible in Settings → AI; can be reset
- Desktop UI specs use Playwright; server/orchestration-layer specs use Vitest

## Files
- `desktop/test/integration/ai-v1/{triage-cleanup,make-startable,brain-dump,failures,token-accounting}.spec.ts`
- `desktop/e2e/ai-v1/{accept-edit-reject.spec.ts}`
- `desktop/test/mocks/anthropic.ts`

## Acceptance
- All ten specs pass with mocks in CI
- Real-AI cassette suite passes locally when `RUN_REAL_AI_TESTS=1` set (uses small prompts to keep cost negligible)
- No test ever hits the real Anthropic API in CI
- Failure paths surface user-visible errors that match PRD §13 wording

## Skills
**Invoke `playwright-electron-debugger`** for the accept-edit-reject Playwright spec (renderer ↔ main IPC, modal focus management).
**Invoke `claude-api`** when implementing the orchestration layer's Anthropic call site — even if mocked here, the real client must use prompt caching, correct model IDs, and the latest SDK patterns.

## Notes
- Ollama and OpenAI flows are NOT exercised here — they're Epic 8 / AI11-test.
- This task does not configure real keys in any environment.

## References
PRD §6 AI Posture, §13 Error states (key/quota/timeout), §16 AI Settings, §17 Cloud Anthropic, §22 Risks (latency, hallucination).

title: F-14a: E2E server fixture — testcontainers Postgres + server lifecycle + dev-mail polling
description:
## Goal
Provide a reusable test fixture that boots a hermetic @calmly/server instance against an ephemeral Postgres (testcontainers) so the F-14 suite (auth/nav/persistence/sync specs) and any future integration tests can drive the real server without touching shared infra.

## Scope
- Add testcontainers + pg deps (devDeps in @calmly/desktop workspace).
- desktop/e2e/fixtures/server.ts:
  * Start a Postgres container (postgres:16-alpine), run server/migrations against it.
  * Boot @calmly/server programmatically via buildApp() on a random port (NODE_ENV=test, EMAIL_SENDER=console, DEV_MAIL_DIR=<tmp>).
  * Return { url, devMailDir, pool, stop() } so specs can teardown deterministically.
- desktop/e2e/fixtures/devMail.ts:
  * pollForMagicLink(devMailDir, email, opts?) — fs.watch / interval poll, parse the link out of the rendered HTML, return string.
- Wire into the existing playwright fixture (electronApp.ts) so a spec opting into 'serverFixture' gets CALMLY_SYNC_URL automatically pointed at the testcontainers URL.
- Add a single 'fixture-smoke.spec.ts' that proves: server boots → /health 200 → POST /auth/request-link → dev-mail file appears with parsable link. NO Electron yet — pure server smoke.

## Acceptance
- pnpm --filter @calmly/desktop test:e2e e2e/fixture-smoke.spec.ts passes locally.
- Container + server cleanly stopped on teardown (no orphaned Postgres after run).
- Tests do not depend on Docker compose / running server.

## Out of scope
- Spinning up Electron (covered by F-14b/c/d/e).
- Multi-tenant isolation (one server per test run is fine).

## Skills
playwright-electron-debugger (fixture authoring) — though Electron itself isn't launched in this bead.

## References
F-14 parent (calmly-2g1.14) decomposition. F-08b will reuse the same testcontainers Postgres pattern at the integration layer.
notes:
LANDED. Server fixture works end-to-end: testcontainers Postgres → node-pg-migrate → spawn @calmly/server (tsx loader) on a pre-allocated port → poll /health → return { url, devMailDir, databaseUrl, stop }. devMail.ts polls the dev-mail dir for new HTML files and parses the magic-link via href regex. fixture-smoke.spec.ts validates the full chain end-to-end (no Electron yet) and self-skips on dev machines without Docker.

Decisions worth recording:
- Pre-allocate the listen port via createServer().listen(0) rather than passing PORT=0 to the server, because server config schema requires PORT > 0. There's a small race window — acceptable for tests, retry on flake.
- Boot detection by polling /health rather than parsing pino JSON output. LOG_LEVEL=warn suppresses fastify's listen log, so log-parsing was fragile.
- node-pg-migrate's '-j cjs' is invalid for the up action in v7+ (only valid for create); .cjs migrations resolve via require() automatically.
- Spawn node-pg-migrate via process.execPath + bin path rather than 'pnpm exec' — pnpm isn't reliably in PATH for nested subshells.
- Keep server fixture surface minimal (no pg pool exposed) until a downstream spec actually needs it.

Local run: 3 specs pass in ~15s (smoke + 2 fixture-smoke tests). Skips gracefully when Docker isn't running.

Unblocks: F-14b (nav), F-14c (auth), F-14d (persistence), F-14e (sync) — all can now use { startServerFixture, pollForMagicLink } from desktop/e2e/fixtures.
close_reason: Landed in c91de31. Server fixture (testcontainers Postgres + server boot + dev-mail polling) verified by fixture-smoke.spec.ts (2 tests pass in ~17s; skips on machines without Docker). Unblocks F-14b/c/d/e.

title: F-08b: Magic-link auth — DB integration tests against real Postgres (testcontainers)
description:
## Goal
Add the full request → redeem → me → logout integration test for F-08 against a real Postgres instance.

## Why this is split from F-08
F-08 lands the schema, crypto, endpoints, middleware, and Vitest unit tests for pure logic (token generation, hashing, expiry, idempotency). The live DB integration test needs F-03's Vitest+testcontainers infra and ideally hooks into CI's Postgres service.

## Scope
- Use @testcontainers/postgresql (or CI service container) to provision Postgres
- Run server migrations against the throwaway DB
- Boot the Fastify app, make HTTP calls
- Assertions:
  - Full happy path: request → email captured → redeem → cookie set → /auth/me OK → logout → /auth/me 401
  - Token expiry: redeem after expires_at returns 410/400
  - Idempotent redeem: second redeem returns same session (or 410 — pick one and pin it)
  - Rate-limit: 6th request in an hour returns 429
  - Cookie flags: HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure in prod
  - Token plaintext never in DB (only sha256 hash)

## Acceptance
- pnpm -r test green with the integration suite

## References
PRD §12, parent F-08.

title: Search: SQLite FTS5 across tasks, inbox, notes
description:
## Goal
Ship a fast keyboard-first full-text search overlay covering tasks, inbox items, and task notes, backed by SQLite FTS5 in the local cache.

## Build order
PRD §23 step 6 (Search).

## Scope
- FTS5 virtual tables for Task title/notes, InboxItem text
- Triggers/handlers to keep FTS in sync on insert/update/delete
- Cmd/Ctrl+K overlay: input, debounced query, ranked result list, keyboard navigation, jump-to-detail
- Result snippeting + highlighting

## Out of scope
- Searching calendar events (calendar is read-only & ephemeral)
- Cross-device search aggregation (local cache only at MVP)

## Done when
Pressing Cmd/Ctrl+K from any screen surfaces a search overlay that returns matching tasks/inbox items/notes within ~50ms on a 10k-item dataset.

## References
PRD §11 Search, §7 desktop item 10, §20 Architecture (local cache).

title: SRCH-01: FTS5 virtual tables + triggers for tasks/inbox/notes (extends F-04)
description:
## Goal
Create FTS5 virtual tables and triggers in the local SQLite cache so tasks, inbox items, and task notes stay fully indexed in real time on insert/update/delete.

## Scope
- Migration extending the F-04 pattern: `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/00xx_search_fts.sql`
- Three FTS5 contentless tables (or `content=` external-content) covering:
  - `task_fts(title, notes, content='task', content_rowid='rowid')`
  - `inbox_fts(text, content='inbox_item', content_rowid='rowid')`
  - Tokenizer: `unicode61 remove_diacritics 2 tokenchars '_-'`
- Triggers on each base table (`AFTER INSERT`, `AFTER UPDATE`, `AFTER DELETE`) that mirror changes into the matching FTS table
- For external-content tables, use `INSERT INTO <fts>(<fts>, rowid, ...) VALUES('delete', old.rowid, ...)` pattern on update/delete
- Wrap insert/update/delete on base tables in transactions so FTS stays consistent
- Typed query helper in `desktop/src/main/search/index.ts`: `searchTasks(q, limit)`, `searchInbox(q, limit)`, `searchAll(q, limit)` returning rowids + ranks
- BM25 ranking via FTS5 `bm25()` function with weight tuning: title weighted 2x notes
- Sanitize FTS5 query syntax: escape user input quotes, append `*` to last token for prefix matching

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/00xx_search_fts.sql`
- `desktop/src/main/search/index.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/search/query.ts` — query sanitizer + ranker
- `shared/src/types/search.ts` — `SearchHit { id, kind, score, snippet? }`

## Acceptance
- Inserting a task with title `"Pay phone bill"` makes `searchTasks('phone')` return that task
- Updating the task title to `"Renew passport"` makes the old query return zero, new query return the task
- Deleting the task removes it from `searchTasks` results
- A query for `pho` (prefix) finds `phone`
- Diacritic-insensitive: query `cafe` finds title `café`
- BM25 ranks title hits above notes-only hits
- Triggers do not fire infinite loops; bulk-insert of 1k tasks completes in under 2s

## Notes
- Backfill of existing rows is srch-backfill — this task only handles forward-going changes via triggers.
- Calendar events are NOT indexed (PRD §11 scope: tasks, inbox, notes).
- AISuggestion content is NOT indexed.
- Use `external content` tables to avoid duplicating row text on disk.

## References
PRD §11 Search, §20 Architecture (local cache + FTS5), §7 desktop item 10.

title: SRCH-02: Backfill existing rows into FTS on first run after upgrade
description:
## Goal
Backfill the FTS index with existing rows on first run after the search migration is applied so users with pre-existing data get search immediately, not only for newly written rows.

## Scope
- Idempotent backfill job triggered once per FTS-related migration version
- Runs after migrations during app boot (main process), but yields to the UI: chunked in batches of 500 rows with `setImmediate` between batches so app startup is not blocked
- Marker stored in `_meta` (or new `_search_meta` table) keyed by FTS migration version: `{version, status, started_at, finished_at, row_count}`
- Status states: `pending` → `running` → `done` (or `error`); on `done` the job is skipped on subsequent boots
- A "Reindex search" button in Settings → Data resets the marker and re-runs the backfill (manual recovery)
- Logs progress to structured logger (F-13) at debug level: every 5k rows
- Concurrency-safe: only one backfill instance per process; if a write happens during backfill, it's safe because triggers are already firing for new writes

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/search/backfill.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/00xx_search_meta.sql` — `_search_meta(version INTEGER PK, status TEXT, ...)`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Settings/Data.tsx` — extend with "Reindex search" button (route placeholder exists from F-06)
- Boot wiring in `desktop/src/main/index.ts` to invoke after migrations

## Acceptance
- First boot after migration with 1k existing tasks + 200 inbox items: all rows are searchable within ~2s of UI being ready, without freezing the renderer
- Second boot does not re-run the backfill (marker is `done`)
- "Reindex search" button completes successfully and re-populates FTS even if base tables were never modified
- Killing the process mid-backfill leaves the marker in `running`; on next boot the job re-starts from row 0 (or resumes — implementation choice; document it)
- An empty database completes backfill instantly with `row_count=0` and `status=done`

## Notes
- Do NOT run backfill on every boot — gate by FTS migration version.
- Reindex button is intentionally low-prominence; this is recovery, not a normal flow.
- Performance test for the 10k dataset is srch-perf-test, not this task.

## References
PRD §11, §20 Architecture, §13 (data integrity recovery).

title: SRCH-03: Search overlay UI (debounced input, ranked list, keyboard nav)
description:
## Goal
Replace the F-06 search overlay placeholder with a real keyboard-first overlay: debounced input, ranked result list, keyboard navigation, and jump-to-detail.

## Scope
- Trigger: Cmd/Ctrl+K from any route opens overlay (already wired in F-06; keep the binding)
- Modal layer: full-screen blur backdrop, centered card; Esc closes; Esc in input also closes (not just clears)
- Input: autofocus on open; debounced 120ms; clears on close
- Result list: max 30 results across all kinds (tasks, inbox, notes-on-tasks); grouped by kind with section headers
- Keyboard nav: ↑/↓ moves selection (wraps at edges), Enter jumps to detail route, Cmd/Ctrl+Enter opens in new context if applicable, Tab cycles section
- Jump-to-detail:
  - Task hit → navigate to `/inbox` or `/plan` and focus that task (use a `pendingFocusId` query param or store)
  - Inbox hit → navigate to `/inbox` and focus item
- Empty state: "Type to search your tasks, inbox, and notes." (no results yet)
- No-results state: "No matches for `<q>`."
- Loading: search calls run in main process via IPC; show subtle spinner only if >150ms
- Overlay state lives outside route tree (singleton) so it can open from anywhere

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/SearchOverlay.tsx` (replace placeholder)
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/search/ResultRow.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/state/searchStore.ts` — open/close, query, results
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/search.ts` — `search(query, limit)` handler
- `desktop/src/preload/search.ts` — `search.query(q)`

## Acceptance
- Cmd/Ctrl+K opens overlay; Esc closes
- Typing "phone" within 200ms (after debounce) populates results from a seeded DB
- ↑/↓ moves selection visually; Enter routes to the correct detail and the target item is visually focused
- Clicking outside the card closes the overlay
- Re-opening preserves no prior input (clean slate)
- No layout shift on the underlying page when overlay opens

## Notes
- Snippeting + highlighting is srch-snippet — show plain titles for now, but make the row component accept an optional snippet prop.
- Performance budget verification is srch-perf-test.
- Calendar events are NOT searchable.
- Do NOT implement saved searches, search history, or filters — out of MVP scope.

## References
PRD §11 Search, §7 desktop item 10, §10 (keyboard-first).

title: SRCH-04: Snippeting + highlighting in result rows
description:
## Goal
Render snippeted, highlighted match context in result rows so users can see why a hit matched without opening the detail.

## Scope
- Use FTS5 `snippet()` function in the search query: `snippet(<fts>, <colidx>, '<mark>', '</mark>', '...', 16)` returning ~16 tokens around the match
- For task hits: prefer snippet from `notes` if the title hit is exact; if title was the match, show full title with highlight; if both match, show title + brief notes snippet
- Inbox hits: snippet from `text`
- Renderer renders `<mark>` segments with a highlight style (no bg color, just bold/underline to keep visual calm)
- Sanitize: snippet output is mostly safe but treat as untrusted; render via a tokenizer that splits on `<mark>` / `</mark>` and creates React fragments — DO NOT use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`
- Long titles are truncated with ellipsis past 80 chars; snippet stays around 120 chars

## Files
- Extend `desktop/src/main/search/index.ts` to return `{ id, kind, score, titleHtml, snippetHtml }` (where `*Html` is actually a structured array of `{ text, highlighted }` segments — name `titleSegments`/`snippetSegments`)
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/search/Highlight.tsx` — segment renderer
- Update `desktop/src/renderer/components/search/ResultRow.tsx` to consume segments
- `shared/src/types/search.ts` — extend `SearchHit` with segments

## Acceptance
- Searching `phone` against a task with notes "remember to pay phone bill before friday" returns a snippet like `…remember to pay <mark>phone</mark> bill before friday…`
- Highlighted segments render bolded (or per chosen style); no raw `<mark>` tags appear in the DOM as text
- A query with no notes and a title hit shows the title with the matched word highlighted
- Snippet length stays within bounds; no layout overflow in the overlay
- Special characters in user content (`<`, `&`, etc.) render as literal text, not HTML

## Notes
- Highlight style intentionally calm per PRD voice — avoid yellow background; use weight or underline.
- Multi-word queries: FTS5 `snippet()` already handles multiple matches; just pass through.
- Do NOT use a JS-side highlighter library — the FTS5 snippet output is sufficient.

## References
PRD §11 Search, §10 (calm voice).

title: SRCH-05: Search performance test (10k rows, p95 < 50ms)
description:
## Goal
Add an automated performance test that verifies search returns results within the PRD budget (~50ms p95) on a 10k-row dataset.

## Scope
- Test harness lives under `desktop/test/perf/search.perf.test.ts` (vitest or node:test — match repo's existing runner)
- Dataset generator: seeds an isolated SQLite DB with 8k tasks (varied title/notes, ~30 tokens avg) + 2k inbox items; deterministic seed for reproducibility
- Runs the FTS index/backfill once; then executes 100 randomized queries (mix of single-token, two-token, prefix queries)
- Records latency per query; asserts p50 < 20ms and p95 < 50ms on a baseline machine; logs full distribution for debugging
- The test is opt-in (skipped by default in normal CI) but runnable via `pnpm --filter desktop test:perf`
- A single CI workflow `perf-search.yml` runs it on push to main and posts a summary to the run log; threshold failure does NOT block PRs (advisory) but DOES fail the workflow status

## Files
- `desktop/test/perf/search.perf.test.ts`
- `desktop/test/perf/seed.ts` — dataset generator
- `desktop/package.json` — add `test:perf` script
- `.github/workflows/perf-search.yml` — opt-in CI job

## Acceptance
- `pnpm --filter desktop test:perf` runs locally and prints a latency report
- p95 latency is under 50ms on a standard dev machine; if not, the test fails with a clear message including the actual p50/p95
- Test isolates its DB to a temp path; does not pollute the user's dev DB
- Re-running with the same seed produces identical row counts (seed determinism)
- Skipped during normal `pnpm test` runs (marked or guarded by env var)

## Notes
- Calibration: thresholds may need tuning per machine class. If CI hardware is slow, adjust the workflow threshold but keep local dev threshold at 50ms.
- Do NOT include this test in the default test suite — it's slow and noisy.
- This test depends on srch-fts-tables and srch-backfill being merged.

## References
PRD §11 Search ("ranked, fast results"), PRD acceptance for fast search; rule of thumb 50ms p95.

title: SRCH-06: FTS5 accuracy + ranking test pass
description:
## Goal
FTS5 accuracy test pass — verify search relevance, ranking, and snippeting against a curated query/expected-result corpus. Complements the perf test in SRCH-05.

## Scope
- Curated dataset: 200 InboxItems + 200 Tasks + 100 Notes covering common ADHD-flavored content (e.g., "buy milk", "pay car rego", "draft Q3 review", "kid's permission slip Tuesday")
- 30 queries with expected top-3 result sets (golden file `desktop/test/fixtures/search/golden.json`)
- Specs (Vitest):
  1. **Exact match**: query "permission slip" returns the permission-slip task in position 1
  2. **Stemming**: query "draft" returns "drafting" / "drafts" hits
  3. **Multi-word**: query "Q3 review" beats unrelated "Q3" or "review" only
  4. **Tokenization**: punctuation stripped (e.g., "kid's" matches "kids")
  5. **Field weighting**: title hits rank above notes hits for same term
  6. **Recency tiebreaker**: among equal-relevance hits, more recent updated_at wins
  7. **Snippet correctness**: returned snippets contain highlighted match terms wrapped in markers
  8. **Empty / very short query**: returns a stable empty result set, not a crash
- Soft regression check: each query's top-3 ordering matches the golden file (allowing per-version golden updates with explicit reviewer sign-off)

## Files
- `desktop/test/integration/search/accuracy.spec.ts`
- `desktop/test/fixtures/search/{corpus.json,golden.json}`

## Acceptance
- All eight spec groups pass
- Golden-file mismatches surface as readable diff, not opaque assertion failure
- Adding a new corpus row doesn't require touching unrelated golden entries

## Skills
None required — this is pure Vitest against the local SQLite cache.

## Notes
- This task complements SRCH-05 (perf test). They run in the same CI job (`e2e-search`).
- Corpus is English-only at MVP; multilingual is out of scope.

## References
PRD §11 Search, §7 desktop item 10.

title: F-03a: Lint + format + Husky + GitHub Actions CI (lint/typecheck/unit jobs)
description:
## Goal
Establish lint, format, and CI infrastructure so every subsequent task can rely on a fast, deterministic check loop. (Playwright + Electron E2E split to F-03b.)

## Scope
- ESLint flat config at root (typescript-eslint + react-hooks + prettier-compatible) — single config covering shared/server/desktop with workspace-specific overrides.
- Prettier config + .prettierignore at root.
- Root scripts: pnpm lint / lint:fix / format / format:check.
- Husky + lint-staged for pre-commit (lint --fix + prettier --write on staged files).
- GitHub Actions CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) with jobs: setup (cache pnpm + node 20), typecheck, lint, format-check, test (workspace-recursive vitest). Linux-only runner, fail-fast off so each job's status is visible.

## Acceptance
- pnpm lint, pnpm format:check, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test all pass on a clean tree.
- ESLint actually flags a deliberate console.log in a sample file, then is fixed.
- CI workflow file passes yamllint and the jobs run in topological order.

## Out of scope
- Playwright + Electron smoke test → F-03b (calmly-cqp). The CI workflow will gain an e2e job there.
- Pre-existing typecheck/test scripts already work; the bead just adds lint/format on top.
notes:
## Approach (F-03a)

### Stack choices
- ESLint v9 flat config (eslint.config.js at repo root) — single config tree with workspace-aware globs. typescript-eslint v8 with recommended (NOT recommended-type-checked initially — that requires per-tsconfig setup that's overhead for the gain). react-hooks for the desktop/renderer glob. eslint-config-prettier disables style rules so prettier owns formatting.
- Prettier with project defaults: 80-char width, double quotes (matches existing code), semis on, trailingComma=all.
- Husky v9 (modern simple init) + lint-staged for pre-commit (lint --fix + prettier --write on staged).
- GitHub Actions: ubuntu runner, pnpm cache, separate jobs typecheck/lint/format-check/test running in parallel after a single setup. fail-fast off so each surfaces independently.

### Tradeoffs / NOT doing
- NOT enabling type-aware lint rules (no-floating-promises etc.) yet — they're ~5x slower and need parser project config per workspace; revisit when test feedback gets noisy.
- NOT pinning rules tightly: starting with a small allowlist of ESLint defaults + typescript-eslint recommended; tighten later as patterns emerge.
- NOT touching the existing test/typecheck scripts; they already work — just extending the surface.
- NOT writing the Playwright + Electron piece — split to F-03b.

### Risk
Existing code may need a few small fixes (unused vars, missing return types) on first lint run. If the volume is non-trivial, document the known violations rather than reflowing across 50 files.
close_reason:
F-03a complete. Lint + format + CI infrastructure landed.

NEW:
- eslint.config.mjs (flat config) at repo root: typescript-eslint recommended (non-type-checked, fast), react-hooks + react-refresh for the renderer, eslint-config-prettier last so formatter rules don't conflict, CJS override for *.cjs migrations, looser rules for tests.
- .prettierrc.json (80/2-space/double-quote/trailing-comma=all/lf) + .prettierignore (long-form docs, generated dirs, lockfile, GUI_draft.ts).
- Root scripts: pnpm lint / lint:fix / format / format:check.
- Lint-staged config in root package.json (eslint --fix + prettier --write on staged ts/tsx/js + json/md/yml).
- .github/workflows/ci.yml: ubuntu-latest with NODE_VERSION=20, PNPM_VERSION=9.12.3, jobs setup (deps cache) → typecheck / lint / format / test in parallel. concurrency.cancel-in-progress on per-ref so superseded runs don't queue.

CHANGED:
- desktop/src/renderer/auth/AuthContext.ts (new) split off from AuthProvider.tsx so react-refresh/only-export-components stops complaining about hooks-next-to-component exports. Consumers (AuthGate, SignIn, Settings/Account) updated.
- desktop/src/main/net/client.ts: replaced `while (true) // eslint-disable` with `for (;;)` (lint preferred).
- 50+ files reformatted by Prettier on first run; no behavioral changes.

PUNTED to F-03c (calmly): Husky pre-commit hook file (.husky/pre-commit). Husky + lint-staged deps + config are wired; only the hook file itself remained, and the .husky directory was permission-restricted in this iteration.

Verified: pnpm lint / pnpm format:check / pnpm -r typecheck / pnpm -r test all green. 178 tests pass (63 shared + 37 server + 78 desktop).

UNBLOCKS F-03b (calmly-cqp): Playwright Electron config + E2E smoke + CI e2e job — needs playwright-electron-debugger skill.

title: F-05b: DB round-trip integration test for core model (Vitest + better-sqlite3)
description:
## Goal
Add the integration test that round-trips one row of every table in the core model through better-sqlite3, validating both the SQL schema and the Zod parsers.

## Why this is split from F-05
F-05 lands the schema and Zod types and verifies the migration applies cleanly on a fresh DB via the Electron-launch smoke test. The proper DB round-trip test needs Vitest infra (provided by F-03) and a Node-ABI better-sqlite3 build separate from the Electron-ABI one used at runtime. Splitting keeps F-05 a single-iteration P0 deliverable and lets the sonnet worker land this once F-03 ships.

## Scope
- Add Vitest to desktop (or wherever the test lives) once F-03 brings the test runner
- Resolve the Node vs Electron ABI rebuild problem (e.g., separate `pnpm rebuild-native:node` script, or use node:sqlite, or run tests under Electron)
- For each table in `0003_core_model.sql`:
  1. Apply migrations to a fresh in-memory DB
  2. Insert one row constructed via the Zod schema (`Schema.parse(...)`)
  3. SELECT the row back, parse via `Schema.parse(row)`, deep-equal compare
- Verify FK cascade: deleting a user removes their inbox/tasks/events/etc.
- Verify CHECK constraints reject invalid enum values

## Acceptance
- `pnpm -r test` runs and passes the integration suite
- One round-trip assertion per table
- One cascade assertion (delete user → child rows gone)
- One CHECK violation assertion (bad enum rejected by DB)

## References
PRD §14, parent F-05.
notes:
LANDED: 14 round-trip integration tests in desktop/src/main/db/__tests__/integration.test.ts.

Engine choice. Used node:sqlite (host Node bundled libsqlite) instead of better-sqlite3 to avoid the Electron-vs-Node ABI rebuild trap. Stable in Node 24+, available behind --experimental-sqlite in 22.5+. Migrations are read directly from the .sql files via fs (no shared runMigrations dependency to keep the test self-contained); foreign_keys=ON pragma applied so the cascade assertion exercises the real FK chain.

Coverage. One round-trip assertion (INSERT a Zod-built row, SELECT, parse back through the schema, assert key fields) for users, inbox_items, tasks (with the schedule pair), events, reminder_rules, recurrence_rules, calendar_event_imports, ai_suggestions, telegram_links, user_settings — every domain table the migrations create. PRAGMA table_info(focus_sessions) check confirms all 8 migrations applied cleanly. FK CASCADE assertion: insert user + inbox + task; delete user; both children gone. Two CHECK violation assertions: bad source enum on inbox_items + bad status enum on tasks both throw.

Tradeoffs. (a) node:sqlite vs better-sqlite3 may diverge on libsqlite version specifics; for schema/Zod portability this is low risk. The comment at the top of the file warns against repurposing for performance assertions. (b) Hand-rolled NodeSqliteDatabase typing locally — avoids bumping @types/node workspace-wide for a test-only API. (c) describe.skipIf(!nodeSqlite) gracefully skips if the host Node lacks the module rather than crashing the whole vitest run. (d) ExperimentalWarning fires on Node 22.x but doesn't affect passes; on Node 24+ the warning goes away.

Verified. Typecheck (web + node) clean; eslint clean on the test; 14 new tests pass; 171 desktop total. No new deps, no engines bump.

This pattern is the template for F-08b (server Postgres integration via testcontainers) and F-11c (multi-client sync E2E).
close_reason: 14 round-trip + cascade + CHECK integration tests landed using node:sqlite. Pattern template for F-08b and F-11c.

title: Electron main process crash: electron-log/main bare specifier
description: F-13b imported electron-log via 'electron-log/main' but Node's strict ESM resolver (used at runtime by Electron's main process) requires the .js extension for subpath imports. electron-vite tolerates the bare specifier at build time, so typecheck and tests pass — but the packaged/dev runtime throws ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on app launch with 'Did you mean to import "electron-log/main.js"?'. title: F-14c: E2E auth.spec.ts — magic-link request → dev-mail poll → deep-link redeem → /auth/me returns user
description:
## Goal
Drive the magic-link auth flow end-to-end through the real server fixture so we catch regressions in the deep-link → token → /auth/me path on every CI run.

## Scope
- desktop/e2e/foundations/auth.spec.ts.
- Steps: launch Electron → SignIn renders → enter test email → POST /auth/request-link via UI → poll devMailDir (F-14a fixture) for the .html → extract magic link → invoke main process app emit('open-url', link) (or send IPC equivalent) → assert renderer flips to signed-in shell → assert window.calmly.auth.status() returns { signedIn: true, user.email }.
- Export a 'signInAsTestUser(electronApp, window, server)' helper that other specs (nav, persistence) can reuse.

## Acceptance

- No flake in 10 consecutive runs (Linux CI).

F-14a (calmly-dmr)
notes:
DESIGN: build desktop/e2e/foundations/auth.spec.ts using existing fixtures (server.ts + devMail.ts + electronApp.ts). Approach: spec-level beforeAll boots startServerFixture(); each test launches Electron with CALMLY_SYNC_URL pointed at the test server (override the base electronApp env). For redeem path, emit 'open-url' on the main-process app via electronApp.evaluate so we exercise the real openUrlHandler → orchestrator.redeem → DEEPLINK_RESULT_CHANNEL → AuthProvider reducer chain. Assert post-redeem: AuthGate flips to children (Home shows 'Peace, friend.') AND window.calmly.auth.status() returns {signedIn:true, user.email}. Helper: export signInAsTestUser(electronApp, window, server, email?) from desktop/e2e/foundations/_helpers.ts so F-14b/d/e reuse the same flow. NOT building it as a Playwright fixture — single-test-per-file ergonomics work fine and avoid the worker/file scope dance.

NOT doing: full route-cycling (F-14b's job), persistence-across-restart (F-14d), multi-client sync (F-14e), happy-only-no-error-paths assertions (the bead is happy-path).

Helper signInAsTestUser exported from desktop/e2e/foundations/_helpers.ts so F-14b/d/e reuse the flow. Self-skips when Docker unavailable. CI's existing e2e job picks it up via *.spec.ts testMatch.

title: Telemetry, onboarding polish, empty/error states
description:
## Goal
Ship opt-in telemetry, complete the empty/error state coverage from PRD §13, and harden onboarding so the deferred-integration model from §12 works in practice.

## Build order
PRD §23 step 9.

## Scope
- Opt-in telemetry pipeline (off by default): feature use counts, session length, AI accept/reject/edit rates, error types — never task content
- Opt-in crash reporting (separate toggle)
- "What is sent" inspector: user can view exact telemetry payload before sending
- Empty states from PRD §13: first open, empty inbox, nothing scheduled, no current focus, review with no completed
- Error states from PRD §13: calendar fail, OAuth expired, Telegram offline / blocked, voice transcription failed, Telegram not linked when expected, sync failed, Ollama not running, key missing/invalid, API failed/timeout, quota exceeded
- Each state: tells user what happened, what to do, whether anything is lost
- Onboarding: 5-min first-run requires only magic-link sign-in; integrations deferred to moment-of-need
- Keyboard shortcuts pass: Cmd/Ctrl+K search, capture hotkey, focus controls, navigation

## Done when
Each integration / failure mode has a tested user-facing state, telemetry can be enabled/inspected/disabled, and a new user can complete first-run in under 5 minutes without configuring any integration.

## References
PRD §12 Onboarding, §13 Empty/Error States, §18 Telemetry.

title: POL-01: Telemetry pipeline (opt-in, allow-listed events, client batching + server ingest)
description:
## Goal
Ship the opt-in telemetry pipeline (off by default) — desktop client batching of allow-listed events and a server ingestion endpoint — so adoption / friction signals can be measured without ever capturing task, calendar, Telegram, or API-key content.

## Scope
- Allow-list of event names (e.g., `app.opened`, `capture.created`, `triage.completed`, `ai.suggestion.accepted|rejected|edited`, `error.shown`) — defined in `shared/src/telemetry/events.ts`
- Strict prop allow-list per event: only booleans, ints, short enum strings, and stable IDs (`anonymous_id`, `session_id`); no free text, no titles, no message bodies
- Client batcher: buffers events in SQLite (`telemetry_outbox` table), flushes every 60s or 50 events when telemetry is enabled; drops silently when disabled
- Anonymous device ID generated on first run (UUID v4), stored in secret store; never tied to user account
- Server endpoint: `POST /telemetry/ingest` accepts batched payloads, validates against the same allow-list, writes to `telemetry_events` table; rejects with 400 on unknown event/prop
- Hard kill switch: setting `telemetry.enabled = false` immediately stops emission AND purges outbox
- Reuse `logger.event` allow-list helper from F-13 as the single emission API

## Files
- `shared/src/telemetry/events.ts` (event + prop schema, Zod)
- `shared/src/telemetry/client.ts` (batcher, flush, allow-list enforcement)
- `desktop/src/main/telemetry/index.ts` (SQLite outbox + flush worker)
- `desktop/migrations/00XX_telemetry_outbox.sql`
- `server/src/routes/telemetry.ts` (ingest endpoint)
- `server/migrations/00XX_telemetry_events.sql`

## Acceptance
- With telemetry off (default), zero network calls to `/telemetry/ingest`; outbox stays empty
- With telemetry on, batched events arrive at server within 60s; payloads strictly schema-validated
- Attempting to emit an unknown event name throws in tests; attempting to attach a non-allow-listed prop throws
- Disabling telemetry mid-session purges outbox and stops further sends
- Server rejects payloads containing fields like `title`, `body`, `message` with 400

## Notes
- This task is the pipeline only; the Settings UI (toggle + inspector) is a separate task (`pol_telemetry_ui`).
- Crash reporting is a separate, independent toggle (`pol_crash_reporting`).
- Keep the anonymous_id rotation policy documented but not user-facing in MVP.

## References
PRD §18 Telemetry (opt-in, captures listed; never captures task/calendar/Telegram content/API keys), §23 step 9, §4 (Trustworthy, transparent).

title: POL-10: Visual regression + a11y + anti-shame copy audit
description:
## Goal
Visual regression and accessibility audit pass — Playwright visual snapshots of every primary screen + axe-core a11y sweep. Locks the design language in place and surfaces accessibility regressions.

## Scope
- **Visual regression**:
  - Playwright `toHaveScreenshot()` snapshots of: Home (empty + populated), Inbox (focused triage), Plan (with events + tasks), Focus (active session + idle), Review (with completed items), Settings (each sub-page), Sign-in
  - Light + dark theme variants (if dark theme implemented; else single mode)
  - Snapshots stored under `desktop/e2e/visual/__snapshots__/`
  - Update flow: `pnpm test:visual --update-snapshots` for intentional changes
- **Accessibility audit**:
  - `@axe-core/playwright` integration; one check per primary screen
  - Zero violations of `wcag2a` and `wcag2aa` rules
  - Manual a11y checklist (in this task's PR description): keyboard-only walkthrough, focus order, screen-reader names for icons

title: POL-02: Telemetry settings UI — toggle + 'what is sent' inspector
description:
## Goal
Build the Settings UI for telemetry — a clear opt-in toggle, a "what is sent" inspector showing the exact payload of buffered events, and the ability to opt out at any time — so users can verify the privacy claim themselves.

## Scope
- Settings → Privacy → Telemetry section
- Toggle: "Help improve Calmly with anonymous usage data" — off by default; copy explains what is + isn't sent in plain language
- "What is sent" inspector: live view of the most recent N (e.g., 50) events currently buffered in the outbox, with raw JSON expandable per event
- Inspector also shows the static allow-list (event names + accepted props) so power users can audit what's possible to send
- "Send a test event now" button (dev/QA aid; gated to non-prod or always-on but harmless)
- Disabling the toggle immediately calls the purge hook from `pol_telemetry_pipeline`
- Link to the public docs page describing the telemetry endpoint (placeholder URL is fine)

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Settings/Privacy/TelemetrySection.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Settings/Privacy/TelemetryInspector.tsx`
- `desktop/src/preload/telemetry.ts` (narrow IPC: `getOutbox`, `getAllowList`, `setEnabled`, `purge`)
- Settings copy in `shared/src/copy/settings.ts`

## Acceptance
- Toggling off purges outbox and stops emission (verified in e2e test)
- Inspector shows real buffered events when telemetry is on; shows empty state with allow-list reference when off
- Copy passes the anti-shame / transparency review: no dark-pattern phrasing, default state is clearly OFF
- Keyboard-accessible: tab order, screen-reader labels on toggle and JSON disclosure controls

## Notes
- Depends on `pol_telemetry_pipeline` for the outbox + purge primitives.
- This is intentionally separate from crash reporting — different toggle, different copy.

## References
PRD §18 Telemetry ("users can inspect what is sent"), §4 (Trustworthy, Anti-shame), §23 step 9.

title: POL-03: Crash reporting (Electron crashReporter, opt-in, separate toggle)
description:
## Goal
Ship opt-in Electron crash reporting as a toggle separate from telemetry, so users can choose to share native crashes (main + renderer) without enabling usage telemetry.

## Scope
- Activate Electron `crashReporter` (configured during F-13 with `uploadToServer: false`); flipping the Settings toggle enables `submitURL` and uploads
- Server endpoint: `POST /crash/ingest` accepts minidump uploads (multipart/form-data); stores blob + metadata to disk or object storage path; no user content beyond stack
- Strip identifiers: no email, no anonymous_id correlation with telemetry events; just `app_version`, `os`, `process_type`
- Settings → Privacy → Crash Reports section: independent toggle with copy explaining what's in a crash report and what isn't
- "View last crash report" button if a dump exists locally (read-only inspector listing file size, timestamp, version)
- Toggle change requires restart to take effect — surface a clear non-modal banner saying "Restart Calmly to apply"
- Default OFF on every fresh install and after migration

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/crash/index.ts` (configure crashReporter, handle restart-required state)
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Settings/Privacy/CrashReportSection.tsx`
- `server/src/routes/crash.ts`
- `desktop/src/preload/crash.ts` (narrow IPC: `getStatus`, `setEnabled`, `getLastReportMeta`)

## Acceptance
- Default OFF; toggling ON + restart begins uploading on next crash
- Toggling OFF prevents any upload after next start; in-flight queued dumps are deleted from local cache
- Crash payload contains no email, no task content, no API keys (verified by test that triggers a renderer crash and inspects the captured file)
- Server endpoint accepts a dump and returns 202; rejects oversized payloads (>10 MB) with 413

## Notes
- Symbol upload + symbolication is out of scope for this task; raw dumps are enough for MVP.
- Settings UI lives next to the telemetry section but the toggles are wholly independent.

## References
PRD §18 Telemetry ("crash reports are separate and also opt-in"), §4 (Trustworthy), §23 step 9.

title: POL-04: Error states pass — calendar, OAuth, Telegram, voice transcription, sync (shared <ErrorState>)
description:
## Goal
Implement consistent, recovery-oriented error states for all integration failures from PRD §13 — calendar fail, OAuth expired, Telegram offline / blocked / not linked, voice transcription failed, sync failed — backed by a shared `<ErrorState>` component so every state answers: what happened, what to do, whether anything is lost.

## Scope
- Build `<ErrorState>` component: icon, headline, body copy, primary action button, optional secondary "learn more" link, optional "loss disclosure" line ("Nothing is lost — your captures are safe locally")
- Variants per integration failure with concrete copy + recovery action:
  - Calendar connection failed (Google or Microsoft) → "Reconnect"
  - Calendar OAuth token expired → "Sign in again"
  - Telegram offline (delivery failed network) → "Retry now"; auto-retry with backoff in background
  - Telegram bot blocked / user removed bot → "Re-link Telegram" with link flow entry point
  - Telegram bot not linked but feature expects it → "Link Telegram" deep link to Settings
  - Voice transcription failed → "Retry transcription" + offer typed fallback for the captured audio
  - Sync failed (local cache out of date) → show last-sync timestamp, "Try again" button; clarify local edits are queued
- Wire each failure code path to render `<ErrorState>` with the right variant; no raw stack traces shown to user
- Each variant emits a telemetry `error.shown` event with `error_type` enum (using the allow-list from `pol_telemetry_pipeline`)

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/ErrorState/ErrorState.tsx`

- Update integration call sites:
  - `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Plan/CalendarPanel.tsx`
  - `desktop/src/main/calendar/oauth.ts` (surface expiry as code)
  - `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Settings/Integrations/Telegram.tsx`

- Every listed failure mode has an automated test that forces the failure and asserts the corresponding `<ErrorState>` variant renders with the right copy + action

title: POL-05: Error states pass — AI / Ollama failures (key, quota, timeout, not running)
description:
## Goal
Implement error states for all AI failure modes from PRD §13 — Ollama not running / model not pulled, API key missing or invalid, API call failed or timed out, API quota exceeded — using the shared `<ErrorState>` component, so AI failures degrade gracefully and never break the deterministic core loop.

description:
## Goal

title: POL-07: Keyboard shortcuts pass (Cmd/Ctrl+K, capture hotkey, focus controls, navigation, docs)
description:
## Goal
Implement and document a coherent keyboard-shortcut layer — global capture hotkey, in-app command palette, focus-session controls, navigation — so the keyboard-first principle is realized.

## Scope
- Global capture hotkey (default `Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + Space`) opens the quick-capture popover from anywhere on the OS; configurable in Settings
- Command palette: `Cmd/Ctrl + K` opens search + actions (jump to page, run command, find a task)
- Navigation: `g h` (Home), `g i` (Inbox), `g p` (Plan), `g f` (Focus), `g r` (Review) — vim-style chord navigation
- Focus session controls: `Space` to start/pause focus timer, `Esc` to end session early, `n` to mark current task done and pick next
- Inbox triage: `j` / `k` to move selection; `Enter` to triage; `1` / `2` / `3` for triage actions
- Settings → Keyboard page: lists every shortcut, allows rebinding the global capture hotkey, reset-to-defaults button
- Help modal: `?` shows context-aware shortcut list for the current page
- All shortcuts respect the focused element (don't fire when typing in an input unless the chord is global)

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/features/shortcuts/registry.ts` (single source of truth for shortcuts + descriptions)
- `desktop/src/renderer/features/shortcuts/useShortcut.ts` (hook + global manager)
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/CommandPalette/CommandPalette.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/ShortcutHelp/ShortcutHelp.tsx`
- `desktop/src/main/globalShortcut.ts` (registers OS-level capture hotkey via Electron `globalShortcut`)
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Settings/Keyboard/KeyboardSection.tsx`

## Acceptance
- Every shortcut listed in the registry is wired and tested; `?` modal renders the full list
- Global capture hotkey opens the capture popover even when Calmly isn't focused
- Rebinding the global hotkey persists across restarts; conflict detection rejects already-claimed combos with a clear message
- Shortcuts don't fire while user is typing in a text input (except global ones)

## Notes
- Mac Cmd vs Windows/Linux Ctrl is handled by a single `mod` token in the registry.
- Accessibility: every shortcut has a non-keyboard equivalent; `?` modal is screen-reader-readable.

## References
PRD §4 Product Principles (Keyboard-first), §12 (low cognitive load), §23 step 9.

title: F-11b: Sync protocol v1 — desktop client (op_queue, sync loop, backoff, offline replay)
description:
## Goal
Wire the desktop side of sync protocol v1 against the server contract that F-11 lands.

## Why this is split from F-11
F-11 ships the protocol types in @calmly/shared/sync, the server-side migration with domain tables + sync columns, and the /sync/pull + /sync/push endpoints with LWW idempotency. The desktop client (op_queue, sync_state, sync loop, exponential backoff, IPC surface) is its own ~3h slice and lands once the server contract is stable.

## Scope
- Desktop migration adds version + deleted_at columns to F-05's domain tables (or builds on a fresh sync schema if cleaner).
- New tables: op_queue(id, table, op, payload_json, created_at, attempts, last_error) and sync_state(last_pulled_version, last_pushed_at).
- desktop/src/main/sync/{client.ts,queue.ts,loop.ts}: HTTP client against the server, queue persistence, background loop driven by network events + 30s tick.
- Backoff: 1s, 2s, 4s, ..., cap 60s on failed push.
- IPC surface: window.calmly.sync.{status, sync()} so the renderer can show a sync indicator and trigger manual sync.

## Acceptance
- Offline write → record lands in op_queue
- Reconnect → queue drains; first failure backs off exponentially
- Pull is idempotent: same since-version returns same records
- pnpm -r test green with sync-loop unit tests (mock HTTP)

## Notes
- Real cross-device E2E (write on client A, read on client B) is F-11c.
notes:
Approach (full F-11b, single iteration):
- Migration 0005_sync_columns.sql: ALTER each of F-05's 9 STRICT domain tables to add `version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` and `deleted_at INTEGER NULL` (SQLite STRICT permits ADD COLUMN when the type is one of the strict types and the new column is NULL or has a literal DEFAULT — our types satisfy both). Plus new STRICT tables: op_queue(id TEXT PK, table_name, op CHECK IN ('upsert','delete'), payload_json, created_at, attempts, last_error) and sync_state singleton (id PK CHECK id=1, last_pulled_version, last_pushed_at).
- src/main/sync/backoff.ts: pure function attempts→delayMs (1s, 2s, 4s, ..., cap 60s) — Vitest-tested as the only easy unit-test.
- src/main/sync/queue.ts + state.ts: take a Database.Database parameter so they're testable without the better-sqlite3 native binding (Electron-ABI ≠ Node-ABI). Real callers pass getDb().
- src/main/sync/client.ts: pull/push wrappers around fetch, sending the calmly_session cookie from Electron's session cookie jar so auth round-trips. Returns parsed PullResponse / PushResponse from @calmly/shared/sync.
- src/main/sync/loop.ts: start/stop background tick; on each tick, drain the queue (push), then pull new since the cursor; on push failure, increment attempts and back off; on pull failure, just retry next tick. Triggered manually via IPC + every 30s + on app online events.
- IPC: window.calmly.sync.{status(), syncNow()} via narrow preload bridge.

Tradeoffs: NOT validating ops against domain schemas before queuing (Zod validation lands when individual mutators are written — the queue is content-agnostic). NOT handling token-refresh / re-auth — when the server returns 401, the loop logs and pauses; F-10 will own re-auth. NOT pursuing per-table cursor — global since-version (server uses one sequence). NOT writing E2E (split: F-11c).
close_reason: Sync protocol v1 desktop client live. Migration 0005_sync_columns.sql adds version (DEFAULT 0) + deleted_at (NULL) to F-05's 9 STRICT domain tables — verified cold-boot logged 'version=5 appliedNow=[1,2,3,4,5]'. Plus new STRICT tables op_queue (id, table_name, op CHECK 'upsert'|'delete', payload_json json_valid, created_at default unixepoch*1000, attempts, last_error) and sync_state singleton (id PK CHECK id=1). queue.ts and state.ts take a Database parameter so they're testable without the better-sqlite3 native binding. backoff.ts is pure math — 1s, 2s, 4s, ..., capped at 60s. client.ts wraps fetch with an injected cookie-header function so Electron's session cookie jar drives auth. loop.ts implements runSyncOnce: drain queue (push), advance cursor (pull), with retry-eligible filtering (rows wait until created_at + backoff(attempts) ≤ now). Accepted/stale/gone results all remove the op (replay-safe); invalid bumps attempts. createSyncLoop wraps it with start/stop/syncNow and a 30s interval. IPC: window.calmly.sync.{status, syncNow}. 12 desktop unit tests (6 backoff + 6 loop) cover happy path, replay safety, error handling, and cursor monotonicity. Typecheck clean. Note: electron-vite externalizeDepsPlugin needed an exclude for @calmly/shared so the schema imports actually bundle. CALMLY_SYNC_URL env var with default localhost:3001 picks the server. Real auth wiring (writing the calmly_session cookie into Electron's session jar after redeem) is F-10's job; multi-client E2E is F-11c (calmly-76j).

title: F-13b: Desktop logging — electron-log file output, renderer→main IPC bridge, crashReporter wiring
description:
## Goal
Wire the desktop side of F-13's logging contract into Electron.

## Why this is split from F-13
F-13 lands the shared scrub regex set, the strict EventProps allow-list, and the server's pino-backed logger. The Electron-specific pieces (electron-log file rotation, renderer→main IPC log bridge, crashReporter init with uploadToServer=false default) deserve their own iteration once the contract is stable, and they need playwright-electron-debugger to verify properly.

## Scope
- Add electron-log to desktop; configure rotating JSON-line file at app.getPath('logs')/calmly.log
- desktop/src/main/logging/index.ts — Logger implementation that calls scrub on all string fields, exposes makeEvent() backed by electron-log
- IPC handler 'log:event' that the renderer's typed bridge calls
- desktop/src/preload/log.ts — narrow typed bridge: only event(name, props), no raw log forwarding
- desktop/src/main/index.ts — call electron crashReporter.start({ uploadToServer: false }) before app.whenReady
- LOG_PII env-gated escape hatch for dev — prod builds hard-disable

## Acceptance
- Cold-boot writes to calmly.log on disk
- Renderer's window.calmly.log.event(...) round-trips to main and lands in the file
- A planted "sk-ant-test123..." string in a log message is replaced with [REDACTED:api_key_anthropic]
- crashReporter.getUploadToServer() returns false by default

## References
F-13, PRD §18.
notes:
## Approach

Reuse the F-13 shared contract verbatim, port to desktop via electron-log.

### Layers
1. desktop/src/main/logging/index.ts — createDesktopLogger({ transport, allowPii }): Logger.
   Mirror of createServerLogger: scrub() on every message + every string field + every event prop value (defense in depth).
2. desktop/src/main/logging/electron-log-transport.ts — configureElectronLog (file path, rotation, JSON-line format) + electronLogTransport(level, msg, fields). Runtime-only — not imported by tests.
3. desktop/src/main/ipc/log.ts — registerLogIpc(logger): only 'log:event'. Renderer cannot forward raw log.{trace,info,...} to keep the IPC surface narrow.
4. desktop/src/preload/log.ts — LogBridge: { event(name, props) } only.
5. desktop/src/main/index.ts — crashReporter.start({ uploadToServer: false }) BEFORE app.whenReady; configureElectronLog() at module scope; create logger + registerLogIpc inside whenReady.

### Testability
The transport is injected. Tests pass a vi.fn capturing records and assert scrub + sanitize behavior without touching electron-log. electron-log itself is exercised manually + future F-14 E2E.

### LOG_PII gate
allowPii = !app.isPackaged && process.env.LOG_PII === 'true'. In packaged builds, LOG_PII is hard-disabled regardless of env value.

### What this is NOT
- No telemetry upload pipeline (Epic 9).
- Not migrating existing console.log calls in main/index.ts — adds one logger.info("boot") to exercise the path; per-call migration is a follow-up.
- crashReporter dump collection only; no upload.
close_reason:
F-13b complete. Desktop logging — electron-log file output, renderer→main IPC bridge, crashReporter wiring.

NEW:
- desktop: electron-log@5.2.0 dependency.
- desktop/src/main/logging/index.ts — createDesktopLogger({transport, allowPii}). Mirrors createServerLogger: scrub on every message + every string field + every event prop value (defense in depth against tokens that fit the EventProps shape regex).
- desktop/src/main/logging/electron-log-transport.ts — configureElectronLog (calmly.log filename, 10 MB rotation, JSON-line format) + electronLogTransport mapping LogLevel→electron-log levels (trace→silly, fatal→error).
- desktop/src/main/ipc/log.ts — registerLogIpc; only 'log:event' (renderer can't dump raw log lines).
- desktop/src/preload/log.ts — LogBridge: { event(name, props) }.
- desktop/src/preload/api-types.ts — LogBridge surfaced on CalmlyApi.
- desktop/src/preload/index.ts — wired log bridge.

CHANGED:
- desktop/src/main/index.ts:
  - crashReporter.start({ uploadToServer: false, productName, submitURL }) BEFORE app.whenReady so even early failures get dumped locally.
  - configureElectronLog() at module scope; createDesktopLogger created with ALLOW_PII = !app.isPackaged && process.env.LOG_PII === 'true' (packaged builds hard-disable PII regardless of env).
  - logger.info("desktop boot", {...}) at module scope to exercise the path on cold start.
  - registerLogIpc(logger) inside whenReady.

TESTS (10 new):
- main/logging/__tests__/logger.test.ts: anthropic key + email scrub in messages, level dispatch, string field scrub (non-strings untouched), undefined fields stay undefined, event records (rejected_props for shape failures, defense-in-depth scrub on strings that DID pass shape validation), allowPii=true bypass for messages/fields/event values.

DEFERRED (out of scope; will land on Sonnet/follow-up):
- Migrating existing console.log calls in main/index.ts to logger.info — this iteration adds one logger.info("boot") to verify the pipeline.
- E2E test that asserts a planted "sk-ant-test123..." string is replaced on disk — F-14's E2E harness will cover it.
- crashReporter.getUploadToServer() runtime assertion — reachable only inside Electron; F-14's harness covers it.

Verified: pnpm -r typecheck clean. pnpm -r test green: 178 total (63 shared + 37 server + 78 desktop). Desktop electron-vite build clean.

UNBLOCKS: nothing strictly (F-14 already unblocked). Closes F-13b deferred from F-13.

title: CL-06c: Plan TaskSidePanel — view/edit task fields from Plan
