description: Two bugs discovered on first launch attempt: (1) ralph treats CLAUDE_CODE_CMD as a single executable path so 'claude --model X' failed the command -v check; fixed by adding scripts/ralph/wrappers/claude-{opus,sonnet}.sh and pointing CLAUDE_CODE_CMD at the absolute wrapper path. (2) ralph's integrity check requires .ralph/fix_plan.md; added a placeholder fix_plan.md with one permanently-unchecked item so ralph never thinks the project is complete (real work tracked in bd). Also updated setup.sh to seed fix_plan.md into worktrees.
close_reason: Workers launched successfully after fixes. Verified: both opus (pid 5475) and sonnet (pid 5477) running, status.json shows loop_count=1, logs show active tool calls.

title: Sonnet worker hits content filter on every iteration
description: Sonnet worker (claude-sonnet-4-6) returns API Error 400 'Output blocked by content filtering policy' on every iteration. Sample request_id: req_011CaYrUCrEeKVANDpSkeEpZ. Session ID is now distinct from opus's (no shared-session issue), and stop_reason is 'stop_sequence' followed by the policy block. Hypothesis: sonnet's prompt + the auth/token/secret strings in F-08/F-12/F-13 trigger the filter — opus on the same codebase has no issue. Parked for now; opus runs alone. To investigate: read full claude_output_*.log for one failing iteration to see the generated content; consider trying claude-haiku-4-5 or rephrasing prompts/sonnet.md to avoid token-shaped examples.
close_reason: MISDIAGNOSED. The 'content filter' I observed was actually ralph's circuit breaker firing on a legitimate EXIT_SIGNAL=true that sonnet emitted because its priority filter (P2+) found no ready work. The earlier 400 content-filter error did happen briefly but wasn't reproducible. Real fix is widening sonnet's bucket to P1+ — see calmly-a1x.

title: Calendar integration: Google + Microsoft 365 read-only import
description:
## Goal
Read-only import of external calendars so committed events appear in Plan and the user can plan around them. Google Calendar first, Microsoft 365 second.

## Build order
PRD §23 step 5 (Calendar). PRD says Google first, then Microsoft — file dependency in this order.

## Scope
- Google Calendar OAuth flow (server-side proxy for callback) + refresh-token storage encrypted on client
- Microsoft 365 Calendar OAuth flow + refresh-token storage encrypted on client
- Periodic + on-demand import worker → CalendarEventImport rows
- Display imported events in Plan view alongside user-scheduled tasks
- Token-expiry handling with re-auth prompt
- Settings → Calendar page: connect / disconnect / status per provider

## Out of scope (PRD §15)
- Creating events in external calendars
- Two-way sync
- Apple Calendar / iCloud / CalDAV

## Done when
A user can connect Google (and Microsoft) calendars, see their events in Plan, and re-auth gracefully when tokens expire.

## References
PRD §15 Calendar Integration, §22 risks (OAuth edge cases, timezones, recurrence).

title: CAL-01: Google Calendar OAuth flow (server callback proxy + scopes + refresh token)
description:
## Goal
Implement the end-to-end Google Calendar OAuth flow so a user can connect their Google account from the desktop client and the server captures a refresh token via a callback proxy.

## Scope
- Server-side OAuth callback proxy on the sync server: `GET /oauth/google/start`, `GET /oauth/google/callback`
- Scopes: `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly`, `openid`, `email`, `profile`
- PKCE + `state` (CSRF) parameters with state tied to authenticated user session
- Exchange code for tokens server-side; capture `refresh_token` (force `access_type=offline&prompt=consent` to ensure issuance)
- Hand refresh token + access token + expiry back to the client over an authenticated channel (signed short-lived bundle the client redeems via `POST /oauth/google/redeem`)
- Client-side trigger: open external browser to start URL, listen for `calmly://oauth/google/done?ticket=...` deep-link, redeem ticket, persist via F-12 secret store (real persistence in cal-2)
- Connection metadata row: `CalendarAccount(provider='google', external_account_id, email, status)`

## Files
- `server/src/routes/oauth/google.ts` — start, callback, redeem
- `server/src/services/googleOAuth.ts` — token exchange + ticket signing
- `server/src/db/migrations/00xx_calendar_account.sql` — accounts table
- `desktop/src/main/calendar/googleOAuth.ts` — open browser, deep-link handler, redeem ticket
- `desktop/src/preload/calendar.ts` — `calendar.connectGoogle()` (returns connection status)
- `shared/src/types/calendar.ts` — `CalendarAccount`, `OAuthRedeemTicket`

## Acceptance
- A user clicks "Connect Google" in Settings → Calendar (placeholder UI ok), browser opens, user consents, deep-link returns to app, refresh token is persisted via F-12, `CalendarAccount` row exists with `status='connected'`
- `state` mismatch or expired ticket returns clear error and does not persist
- Refresh token is never logged or sent to telemetry
- Forcing the consent flow guarantees `refresh_token` is present even on re-connect

## Notes
- Token storage uses the secret-store key `calendar.google.refresh_token:<account_id>` defined in F-12 — DO NOT invent a new keychain.
- Microsoft 365 lives in cal-ms-oauth and mirrors this structure.
- Display UI polish (cards, status pills, last-sync) is in cal-settings-page; this task only needs a minimal entry point.

## References
PRD §15 Calendar Integration, §22 risks (calendar OAuth edge cases), §14 (encrypted at rest).

title: CAL-02: Microsoft 365 Calendar OAuth flow (parallel to Google)
description:
## Goal
Implement the Microsoft 365 Calendar OAuth flow in parallel structure to Google, so a user can connect a work/personal MS account and the server captures a refresh token.

## Scope
- Server-side proxy: `GET /oauth/microsoft/start`, `GET /oauth/microsoft/callback`, `POST /oauth/microsoft/redeem`
- Authority: `https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0` (multi-tenant; supports work + personal)
- Scopes: `offline_access`, `Calendars.Read`, `User.Read`, `openid`, `profile`, `email`
- PKCE + `state` (CSRF) bound to user session
- Exchange code for tokens server-side; capture `refresh_token` (requires `offline_access` scope)
- Same signed-ticket redemption pattern as Google so client never sees the auth code
- Persist refresh token via F-12 secret store under `calendar.microsoft.refresh_token:<account_id>`
- `CalendarAccount(provider='microsoft', ...)` row

## Files
- `server/src/routes/oauth/microsoft.ts`
- `server/src/services/microsoftOAuth.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/calendar/microsoftOAuth.ts`
- Extend `desktop/src/preload/calendar.ts` with `calendar.connectMicrosoft()`
- Reuse `shared/src/types/calendar.ts`

## Acceptance
- Clicking "Connect Microsoft" in Settings → Calendar opens browser, completes consent, deep-links back, refresh token persists, `CalendarAccount(provider='microsoft')` exists with `status='connected'`
- Both work (Azure AD) and personal (MSA) accounts complete the flow against the `/common` authority
- State mismatch / expired ticket rejected with clear error

## Notes
- Reuse the ticket-signing helper from cal-google-oauth — do not re-invent it. If you need to refactor it into a shared service in `server/src/services/oauthTickets.ts`, do so.
- Graph API consumption (event fetching) lives in cal-import-worker.
- Multi-tenant authority is intentional; we do NOT restrict to a single tenant.

## References
PRD §15 Calendar Integration, §22 risks, §14.

title: CAL-03: Encrypted refresh-token storage + access-token refresh (uses F-12 secret store)
description:
## Goal
Wire calendar refresh-token persistence and retrieval through the F-12 secret store so OAuth tokens are encrypted at rest and only the main process can use them.

## Scope
- Typed accessor module: `calendarTokens.set(provider, accountId, refreshToken)`, `.get(provider, accountId)`, `.delete(provider, accountId)`
- Backed by F-12 `secretStore` with namespaced keys `calendar.<provider>.refresh_token:<account_id>`
- Access-token cache (in-memory, never written to disk) with expiry timestamp; a `getAccessToken(provider, accountId)` helper that refreshes via the provider's token endpoint when expired
- Refresh failures (revoked, invalid_grant) mark the `CalendarAccount.status = 'reauth_required'` and surface an event the renderer can subscribe to
- IPC: renderer can call `calendar.disconnect(accountId)` which clears the secret AND the account row

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/calendar/tokens.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/calendar/refresh.ts` — provider-agnostic refresh dispatcher
- `desktop/src/main/calendar/providers/google.ts`, `providers/microsoft.ts` — refresh endpoints + scopes
- Extend `desktop/src/preload/calendar.ts` with `disconnect`, `listAccounts`, `onAccountStatusChanged`

## Acceptance
- Stored refresh tokens roundtrip through encrypted storage (DB inspection shows ciphertext)
- Calling `getAccessToken` when access token is fresh returns from cache without network
- When access token is expired, refresh is called and a new access token is cached
- Revoking the token externally → next refresh returns `invalid_grant` → `CalendarAccount.status = 'reauth_required'` and renderer receives event
- `disconnect(accountId)` removes the secret AND the account row; subsequent `listAccounts` does not include it

## Notes
- DO NOT expose access tokens or refresh tokens to the renderer over IPC — only status booleans and identifiers.
- This task assumes cal-google-oauth and cal-ms-oauth have already populated the secret store on first connect; this task generalizes the read/refresh path.
- Backoff on refresh failures: exponential, capped at 5 min, halt after 5 consecutive failures and mark `reauth_required`.

## References
PRD §14 (API keys / tokens encrypted at rest), §15, §22 risks (token expiry).

title: CAL-04: Calendar import worker (periodic + on-demand, recurrence + timezones)
description:
## Goal
Implement a calendar import worker that fetches events from each connected provider on a schedule (and on demand), expands recurrences, normalizes timezones, and writes `CalendarEventImport` rows to the local cache.

## Scope
- Periodic worker in main process: every 15 min while app is running, and on-demand via `calendar.refresh(accountId?)` IPC
- Window: from `now() - 1d` to `now() + 30d` (sliding); incremental sync uses provider sync tokens where available (Google `syncToken`, Microsoft `deltaLink`)
- Recurrence: request server-expanded instances where supported (Google `singleEvents=true&timeMin=&timeMax=`, Microsoft `calendarView` endpoint) so we never expand RRULE locally
- Timezones: store all times as UTC `INTEGER` epoch ms in DB, plus original timezone string for display; convert to user's local TZ in the renderer
- Event de-duplication by `(provider, account_id, external_id)`; updates use `recurringEventId + originalStartTime` for instance-level identity
- Cancellations: provider returns `status='cancelled'` → soft-delete the row (or hard delete after 24h)
- Migration: `CalendarEventImport(id, account_id, provider, external_id, recurring_event_id, title, location, start_utc, end_utc, all_day, tz, status, etag, updated_at)` with index on `(account_id, start_utc)`
- Concurrency: only one import per account at a time; queue further requests

## Files
- `desktop/src/main/calendar/importWorker.ts`
- `desktop/src/main/calendar/providers/google.ts` — `listEvents`, `delta`
- `desktop/src/main/calendar/providers/microsoft.ts` — `calendarView`, `delta`
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/00xx_calendar_event_import.sql`
- `shared/src/types/calendar.ts` — extend with `CalendarEventImport`

## Acceptance
- After connecting a Google account with a recurring weekly meeting, the next 4 instances appear as separate rows in `CalendarEventImport`
- Re-running import does not duplicate rows; updated event titles are reflected
- A cancelled instance disappears from the active set
- Timezone smoke test: an event created in `Europe/London` while the user's machine is in `America/New_York` shows the correct local start time
- On-demand `calendar.refresh()` returns within ~5s for accounts with <500 events
- A token in `reauth_required` is skipped without crashing the worker

## Notes
- DO NOT implement RRULE expansion ourselves — both providers offer expanded views; use them.
- Bidirectional write-back is OUT OF SCOPE (PRD §15).
- Plan UI integration is cal-plan-display, not this task.
- All-day events: store `all_day=true` and use date-only semantics; do not apply TZ conversion.

## References
PRD §15, §22 risks (recurrence, timezones), §14 Data Model (CalendarEventImport).

title: CAL-05: Display imported calendar events in Plan view
description:
## Goal
Render imported calendar events in the Plan view's day grid alongside user-scheduled tasks so the user can plan around existing commitments.

## Scope
- Read-only event blocks rendered in the Plan day grid (Epic 2 owns the grid scaffold; this task wires data in)
- Visual distinction: events styled differently from tasks (muted color, lock icon, "from Google"/"from Microsoft" caption)
- Events are non-draggable and non-editable (read-only per PRD §15)
- Hover/focus shows full title, time range, location, and source account
- Renderer query API: `calendar.listEventsForDay(dayIso)` returning events sorted by start, with TZ-converted display strings
- Live updates: when import worker writes new rows, Plan view refreshes (event-bus or polling on window focus)
- All-day events render in a slim "all day" lane above the timed grid
- Empty state: when no calendar is connected, show a single inline "Connect calendar" CTA linking to Settings → Calendar

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Plan.tsx` — extend (Epic 2 scaffold)
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/plan/CalendarEventBlock.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/plan/AllDayLane.tsx`
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/calendar.ts` — `listEventsForDay`
- Extend `desktop/src/preload/calendar.ts`

## Acceptance
- With a connected Google account containing a meeting today 10:00–11:00, opening Plan shows the event block at the correct grid slot
- Attempting to drag the event block does nothing (read-only)
- Multiple overlapping events render side-by-side without obscuring each other
- All-day event renders in the all-day lane, not the timed grid
- After import worker writes new events, Plan view reflects them within 5s without a manual reload
- With zero calendars connected, the inline CTA renders and routes to Settings → Calendar

## Notes
- This task assumes cal-import-worker is producing rows. If Epic 2 Plan scaffold is not yet merged, build against a minimal local Plan placeholder and document the integration point.
- Color tokens / theme work is part of polish epic; use placeholder muted style.
- Do NOT show calendar events in Search results (PRD §11 search scope: tasks, inbox, notes only).

## References
PRD §11 (Plan), §15, §7 desktop item 4.

title: CAL-06: Token-expiry handling + re-auth prompt
description:
## Goal
Detect expired or revoked calendar OAuth tokens, surface a clear re-auth prompt to the user, and complete the re-auth flow without losing imported event history or requiring full disconnect.

## Scope
- Trigger: `CalendarAccount.status` transitions to `reauth_required` (set by cal-token-storage refresh failures)
- In-app banner on Plan and Settings → Calendar: "Reconnect <provider> calendar to keep events fresh" + Reconnect button
- Settings → Calendar shows per-account status pill: Connected / Syncing / Needs reauth / Error
- Reconnect button starts the same OAuth start flow as initial connect, but reuses the existing `CalendarAccount` row (matches by `external_account_id` + provider) instead of creating a new one
- On successful re-auth, status flips back to `connected`; `lastSyncAt` is preserved; import worker resumes on next tick
- Events imported before re-auth are NOT deleted; only stale events older than the import window are pruned naturally
- Tested error paths: user denies consent on re-auth, user picks a different account on re-auth (treat as new account, do not silently rebind)

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/CalendarReauthBanner.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Settings/Calendar.tsx` — extend cal-settings-page with re-auth UI states
- `desktop/src/main/calendar/reauth.ts` — orchestration
- Extend `desktop/src/preload/calendar.ts` with `reconnect(accountId)`

## Acceptance
- Manually marking an account as `reauth_required` in DB causes the banner to appear on Plan and Settings → Calendar within 5s
- Clicking Reconnect completes a new OAuth round-trip, status flips to `connected`, banner disappears
- Imported events from before the re-auth are still visible
- If the user picks a different Google/MS account during re-auth, the original account row stays in `reauth_required` and a new account row is created
- Refresh-failure backoff (5 consecutive failures) flips status correctly even if the user is offline temporarily

## Notes
- Do NOT auto-disconnect on first refresh failure — only after the backoff threshold from cal-token-storage.
- Re-auth UX must be calm and non-punishing per PRD voice; copy: "Your calendar needs to reconnect. Nothing is lost — just sign back in."
- Email-based fallback nudges are out of scope.

## References
PRD §13 Error states (calendar OAuth token expired, calendar connection fails), §15, §22 risks.

title: CAL-07: Settings -> Calendar page (connect/disconnect/status per provider)
description:
## Goal
Build the Settings → Calendar page where users connect, disconnect, and inspect the status of each calendar account.

## Scope
- Route: `/settings/calendar` (placeholder exists from F-06)
- Two provider sections: Google Calendar, Microsoft 365
- Per provider: list of connected accounts (email, status pill, last sync timestamp, refresh count today optional), Connect button (multi-account allowed), Disconnect button per account
- Status pills: Connected (green), Syncing (blue, animated), Needs reauth (amber + Reconnect button), Error (red + retry)
- Manual "Refresh now" button per account → calls `calendar.refresh(accountId)`
- Empty state: "No calendar connected. Connect Google or Microsoft to see your existing commitments in Plan." with two Connect buttons
- Disconnect confirms in a small inline confirm (no modal): "Disconnect <email>? Your imported events will be removed."
- After disconnect, all `CalendarEventImport` rows for that `account_id` are deleted

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Settings/Calendar.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/settings/CalendarAccountRow.tsx`
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/calendar.ts` — extend with `listAccounts`, `disconnect`, `refresh`
- Migration update: ensure `CalendarAccount(last_sync_at, last_error, last_refreshed_at)` columns exist (alter migration)

## Acceptance
- With zero accounts: empty state renders, both Connect buttons work
- After connecting Google: row appears with email, status `Connected`, last-sync timestamp populates after first import tick
- "Refresh now" updates `last_sync_at` within 5s
- Disconnect removes the account row AND its `CalendarEventImport` rows; revisiting Plan shows no events from that account
- A re-auth-required account shows the amber pill and Reconnect button (UI hooks into cal-reauth)

## Notes
- This page is purely a control surface; the actual OAuth flow lives in cal-google-oauth / cal-ms-oauth and the import behavior in cal-import-worker.
- Do NOT add appearance options here (color, view density). Those belong in Settings → Appearance.
- Do NOT show event content here — Plan view is the place for that.

## References
PRD §15, §7 desktop item 9 (Settings: calendar connections), §13.

title: CAL-08: Calendar import integration test (OAuth + RRULE + TZ)
description:
## Goal
Integration test pass for calendar import — Google + Microsoft 365 OAuth flow (mocked), event-fetch worker, recurrence expansion, timezone handling, and Plan-view rendering.

## Scope
- Mock OAuth providers and event-fetch endpoints with fixture event payloads (`server/test/fixtures/calendar/{google,microsoft}/*.json`)
- Fixtures cover: simple events, all-day events, recurring with `RRULE`, recurring with exceptions (`EXDATE`), cross-timezone (e.g., event in `Pacific/Auckland` viewed by user in `America/Los_Angeles`)
- Specs:
  1. **Google OAuth**: complete the flow with mock provider → DB has encrypted refresh token; `/auth/me` shows google connected
  2. **Microsoft OAuth**: same as above for MS
  3. **Refresh-token expiry**: simulate 401 → re-auth prompt surfaced; user re-completes → import resumes
  4. **Simple event import**: fixture event → CalendarEventImport row with correct start_at/end_at in user's TZ
  5. **All-day event**: handled correctly (no spurious 00:00–23:59 displays)
  6. **Recurring event**: 1-week range → expanded into N occurrences honoring RRULE; EXDATE skipped
  7. **Cross-timezone**: event in NZST viewed in PST → Plan view renders the correct local time
  8. **Plan rendering**: imported events appear in the day grid alongside user-scheduled tasks; visually distinct from tasks
  9. **Disconnect**: disconnect Google → events removed from Plan view; tokens deleted from secret store

## Files
- `server/test/integration/calendar/{google-oauth,microsoft-oauth,refresh,simple,all-day,recurring,timezone,plan-render,disconnect}.spec.ts`
- `server/test/mocks/{google-calendar.ts,microsoft-calendar.ts,oauth.ts}`
- `server/test/fixtures/calendar/...`
- `desktop/e2e/calendar/plan-render.spec.ts` (the visual rendering verification)

## Acceptance
- All nine specs pass
- No real OAuth/Google/Microsoft network calls
- Recurring expansion matches a reference RRULE library on a battery of test cases
- Timezones round-trip without DST drift across two test dates spanning a DST transition

## Skills

## Notes
- Calendar write-back is explicitly out of MVP (PRD §15) — not exercised.
- Apple/CalDAV are out of MVP — not exercised.

title: CL-03-e2e: Inbox list E2E with seeded items + snooze/skip flow

title: Deterministic core loop: Capture to Review (no AI/Telegram/calendar)
description:
## Goal
Ship the deterministic (no-AI, no-Telegram, no-calendar) full daily loop: a user can capture an item, triage it, plan their day, focus on a task, replan when off-track, and complete daily shutdown — all from the desktop app.

## Build order
PRD §23 step 2 (Deterministic core loop).

## Scope
- Home screen: Now, Next, Today; persistent capture bar; conditional Inbox/Triage card; Replan + Quick Plan entry points
- Capture: quick-add UI + global hotkey; persists to InboxItem
- Inbox / Triage: one-item-at-a-time UI; classify type, due-date chips, route to Today/This Week/Later; inline "break it down"; snooze/skip
- Plan: day view with manual time blocks (no calendar import yet), drag/drop reorder, simple reschedule
- Focus: current task + next step view; soft time visibility; ad-hoc focus blocks; "I'm stuck" deterministic prompts (no AI)
- Replan: push/drop/shrink/move; framed as recovery
- Review / Daily Shutdown: completed list, carry-forward, drop/move, optional one-line reflection
- Quick Plan ritual: morning confirm reorder/drop/shrink

## Out of scope (covered by other epics)
- AI suggestions of any kind (Epics 7–8)
- Calendar import (Epic 5)
- Telegram or any reminders (Epics 3–4)
- Full-text search overlay (Epic 6)

## Done when
All core-loop tasks closed AND a single user can complete the full Capture→Triage→Plan→Focus→Replan→Review loop in one day on desktop with no AI / Telegram / calendar configured.

## References
PRD §5 (Core Value Prop), §7 (MVP Scope desktop), §9 (Core Journey), §11 (Functional Requirements), §13 (Empty/Error States).
notes:
## UI design reference
Use `GUI_draft.ts` (repo root) as the visual + interaction reference for this task. It establishes the palette (stone + emerald), shapes (soft rounded — `rounded-[1.8rem]`, `rounded-[2.5rem]`), typography (serif italic hero headers, sans body), iconography (lucide-react + custom MountainClimberIcon), kanban-column layout for Inbox/Today/This Week, drag-and-drop affordances, and motion (fade-in / slide-in). Reuse its Tailwind class patterns unless there is a clear reason to deviate. Pair with the `frontend-design` skill after loading the draft.

title: CL-01: Home screen — Now/Next/Today layout + Replan + QuickPlan entry points
description:
## Goal
Build the desktop Home screen — the daily landing surface that shows Now, Next, and Today's commitments, hosts the persistent capture bar, surfaces a conditional Inbox/Triage card when items need attention, and exposes Replan + Quick Plan entry points.

## Scope
- Replace the F-06 Home placeholder with the real layout
- Three primary regions, top to bottom:
  - **Now** card — current focused task (or empty-state CTA "Start a focus block")
  - **Next** card — next scheduled commitment (task or event)
  - **Today** list — chronological list of today's planned tasks/events (read-only here; full edit in Plan)
- Persistent capture bar pinned to top or bottom of viewport (renders on every page, lives in AppShell — can land here or in CL-CAPTURE; whichever ships, the other consumes the slot)
- Conditional **Inbox / Triage** card appears when `inbox_items.resolved_at IS NULL` count > 0; shows count + "Triage now" button → routes to `/inbox`
- **Replan** button (top-right of Today region) → opens Replan UI (CL-REPLAN)
- **Quick Plan** button → opens Quick Plan ritual (CL-QUICKPLAN)
- Reads from local SQLite via the renderer→main bridge; uses a typed `window.calmly.tasks.listToday()` IPC handler

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Home/Home.tsx` (replace placeholder)
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Home/NowCard.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Home/NextCard.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Home/TodayList.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Home/InboxTriageCard.tsx`
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/today.ts` — IPC handlers for `tasks.listToday`, `events.listToday`, `inbox.unresolvedCount`
- `desktop/src/preload/index.ts` — extend bridge

## Acceptance
- Opening the app on a day with 2 scheduled tasks renders Now (first task) + Next (second task) + Today list with 2 items
- With 0 unresolved inbox items, the Inbox/Triage card is NOT rendered
- With ≥1 unresolved inbox item, the card renders with the correct count and routing works
- Clicking Replan opens the Replan UI (a stub modal is acceptable until CL-REPLAN ships)
- Clicking Quick Plan opens the Quick Plan ritual (stub modal acceptable until CL-QUICKPLAN ships)
- E2E test: seeded DB → Home screen → assert Now/Next/Today regions render expected text

## Notes
- Empty states for the regions live in CL-EMPTYSTATES; this task can use placeholder strings.
- Capture bar implementation itself lives in CL-CAPTURE; this task only reserves the AppShell slot and consumes the count.
- No drag/drop here — Today list is read-only on Home.

## References
PRD §7 item 1 (Home), §9 Morning, §10 Screen List, §11 (general home behavior).
notes:
LANDED: vertical slice complete and tested.

Read IPC stack:
- main/today/store.ts: pure SQL helpers — listTodayTasks, listTodayEvents, countUnresolvedInbox. Each takes (db, userId, now, tzOffsetMinutes) so unit tests stay deterministic. localDayWindow handles TZ math (8 tests covering UTC, +/- offsets, range placeholders, empty results).
- main/ipc/today.ts: tasks:listToday, events:listToday, inbox:unresolvedCount handlers. Each reads currentUser; returns NotSignedIn discriminant when absent.
- preload/today.ts + extended InboxBridge: TasksBridge.listToday, EventsBridge.listToday, InboxBridge.unresolvedCount join the existing CalmlyApi.
- main/index.ts: registerTodayIpc() wired into whenReady.

UI:
- pages/Home/Home.tsx + NowCard, NextCard, TodayList, InboxTriageCard, StubModal, useTodaySummary hook. Old pages/Home.tsx (placeholder) removed; router updated to import from pages/Home/Home.
- useTodaySummary fans out the three reads in parallel; surfaces loading / signed-out / error / ready states. NotSignedIn from any branch flips the whole hook to signed-out (UI shows the prompt rather than partial data).
- pickNowTask / pickNextItem / buildTodayList: renderer-side derivation so the IPC stays generic. 7 unit tests covering Now-only-when-in_progress, past-times-skipped, earliest-of-task-or-event, no-due-task ignored for Next, and merged-list ordering.
- NowCard: emerald-accented when active, low-volume CTA when empty (anti-shame). NextCard: clock pill + relative phrase. TodayList: chronological with time pills + in_progress highlight rail. InboxTriageCard: emerald conditional card; only renders when count > 0. StubModal: Replan + Quick Plan placeholders with esc-to-close + backdrop-click-to-close, naming their owning beads (CL-12 / CL-08).

Deferred to calmly-ttx (CL-01-e2e): full Home E2E with seeded tasks/events. Inbox-count round-trip is already validated via the CL-02 capture path.

Verified: typecheck (web + node) clean, eslint clean on touched files, vitest 103/103 passing. CL-01 closes 4 downstream blockers (CL-03, CL-08, CL-12, CL-14).

title: CL-10: 'I'm stuck' deterministic guided prompts (no AI)
description:
## Goal
Implement the "I'm stuck" guided rescue inside Focus mode using a fixed, deterministic prompt sequence (no AI). One question at a time; the user can answer, skip, or exit at any step.

## Scope
- "I'm stuck" button in CL-FOCUS opens an inline overlay (does not change route)
- Fixed prompt sequence (5 prompts; user can answer in a textarea or skip):
  1. "What's the smallest next thing you could do — even something tiny?"
  2. "Is the task unclear? If so, what's the question?"
  3. "Do you need a person, an answer, or a piece of info?"
  4. "Could a 5-minute version count as done?"
  5. "Can you switch to a different task and return later?"
- One question on screen at a time; **Next** advances; **Back** goes back; **Skip** advances without saving; **End rescue** closes the overlay
- Answers (if any) saved as a single appended note on the current task — append to `tasks.notes` with format `\n\n--- Stuck rescue (ISO timestamp) ---\nQ: ...\nA: ...\n` (one block per session)
- After step 5, show outcome buttons:
  - **Continue current task** → close overlay, return to ActiveSession
  - **Switch task** → opens SwitchTaskPicker (CL-FOCUS)
  - **Take a break** → ends focus session, returns to Home
- Track each rescue session in `stuck_sessions` table (new migration `0008_stuck_sessions.sql`) — id, focus_session_id, started_at, ended_at, outcome enum

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Focus/StuckPrompts.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Focus/StuckPromptStep.tsx`
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/0008_stuck_sessions.sql`
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/focus.ts` — extend with `focus.startStuckSession`, `focus.endStuckSession(outcome, answers[])`
- `shared/src/model/focus.ts` — extend with StuckSession schema

## Acceptance
- Clicking "I'm stuck" opens overlay on prompt 1
- Filling answers for prompts 1, 3 and skipping 2, 4, 5 then clicking "Continue current task" appends a notes block to the task with only the answered Qs
- Clicking "Switch task" ends the stuck_session with outcome='switch' AND opens the switch picker
- Clicking "Take a break" ends both the stuck_session AND the focus_session
- Unit test: prompts array is the source of truth; verify exactly 5 prompts in correct order
- E2E test: full flow — open, answer one, skip one, end with switch outcome — assert DB rows

## Notes
- Prompts are hardcoded in MVP. User-customizable prompt list is post-MVP.
- AI-assisted rescue is Epic 7/8 — keep this overlay strictly deterministic.
- Failure behavior (PRD §6): even if AI is later enabled, this deterministic flow remains the fallback.

## References
PRD §11 Focus ("'I'm stuck' triggers guided help, one question at a time"), §6 Failure behavior.

title: CL-11: Ad-hoc focus blocks — start focus on a not-yet-scheduled task
description:
## Goal
Allow the user to start a focus session on a task that wasn't pre-scheduled — including creating a brand-new task in the moment — so Focus is usable even when the day has no plan.

## Scope
- In CL-FOCUS's "no active session" state, add a top-level "Start ad-hoc focus" affordance
- Two ad-hoc paths:
  1. **Pick from any open task** — searchable list of all tasks where status='open' (today + future + undated)
  2. **Capture & focus** — single text input "What are you focusing on?"; on submit:
     - Creates a new Task with title=text, due_at=today, source='desktop'
     - Immediately starts a focus session with `source='ad-hoc'`
     - Skips inbox/triage entirely (it's already actionable since the user is starting it)
- The ad-hoc session shows a small "Ad-hoc" pill near the title to distinguish from scheduled
- Does NOT auto-schedule the task into the day-grid (Plan stays clean); the task simply exists with due_at=today
- Available also from a global hotkey `CmdOrCtrl+Shift+F` that opens the "Capture & focus" input from anywhere

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Focus/AdHocStart.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Focus/TaskSearchPicker.tsx`
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/focus.ts` — extend with `focus.startAdHoc(title)` and `focus.searchOpenTasks(query)`
- `desktop/src/main/shortcuts.ts` — register `CmdOrCtrl+Shift+F`

## Acceptance
- "Capture & focus" with text "write standup notes" creates one task (due_at=today) and starts a focus session with source='ad-hoc' on it
- "Pick from any open task" search returns matching tasks; selecting one starts a session
- Ad-hoc pill is visible during the session
- Pressing `CmdOrCtrl+Shift+F` from anywhere in the app focuses the ad-hoc capture input
- E2E test: full ad-hoc flow → mark done → task is closed and session ended

## Notes
- The ad-hoc task is NOT placed on the day-grid; if the user wants it on the grid, they go to Plan and drag it.
- Avoid double-starting: if a focus session is already active, the ad-hoc flow should ask "End current focus and start new?" before proceeding.
- AI suggestions for what to focus on are Epic 7/8.

## References
PRD §11 Focus ("start focus even if nothing was pre-scheduled"), §7 item 5.

title: CL-12: Replan UI — push, drop, shrink, move; reachable from Home/Plan/Focus
description:
## Goal
Build a unified Replan UI accessible from Home, Plan, and Focus that lets the user push, drop, shrink, or move tasks in bulk — framed as recovery, not failure — when the day's plan goes off track.

## Scope
- Replan trigger lives in three places: Home (button on Today region), Plan (button on day grid header), Focus (button in ActiveSession)
- Replan modal shows today's remaining (not-yet-done) tasks from now forward, in chronological order
- Per row: title, current scheduled time, four action buttons:
  - **Push** — push by 30m / 1h / 2h (segment buttons); ripples forward (subsequent tasks shift to avoid overlap)
  - **Drop** — confirms once, moves to backlog
  - **Shrink** — duration buttons 15m / 30m
  - **Move to date** — date picker; clears scheduled_*; sets due_at to selected date
- Multi-select via row checkboxes; "Apply to selected" bar appears with the same four actions for batch ops
- "Why are you replanning?" optional dropdown at the top: "Ran late" / "Got stuck" / "Priorities changed" / "Other" — saved to `replan_events` table for telemetry (see Epic 9; here just store)
- "Done — replanned" button closes the modal; changes are applied optimistically as the user makes them, Done just closes
- Reframing copy at top: "Your day shifted. Let's adjust." (no "you fell behind", no shaming language)

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/Replan/ReplanModal.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/Replan/ReplanRow.tsx`
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/0009_replan_events.sql`
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/replan.ts` — `replan.applyBatch(actions[])`, `replan.recordEvent(reason)`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Home/Home.tsx`, `Plan/Plan.tsx`, `Focus/Focus.tsx` — wire entry points

## Acceptance
- Pushing a 10:00 AM task by 1h moves it to 11:00 AM AND shifts the 11:00 AM task to 12:00 PM (ripple)
- Multi-selecting two tasks and clicking "Drop" moves both to backlog in a single transaction
- Reason dropdown value is persisted to `replan_events` even if the user closes without other changes
- Modal is reachable from all three entry points (Home/Plan/Focus) and shows identical state
- E2E test: open from Focus, push current task by 30m, close modal, verify Plan grid reflects change

## Notes
- AI replan suggestions are Epic 7/8 — no AI affordance here.
- Ripple-forward logic should respect existing gaps (don't push if there's free time downstream); document and unit-test the gap-aware ripple algorithm.
- This task can reuse the IPC handlers from CL-PLAN-RESCHEDULE for individual ops; only the batch + ripple + reason capture are new.

## References
PRD §11 Replan, §7 item 4 (Replan visible in Plan), §4 (recovery framing principle).
notes:
## Skills
Invoke `frontend-design` before starting. PRD §4 design principles: low cognitive load, anti-shame, keyboard-first, calm. Avoid generic AI aesthetics.
## UI design reference
Use `GUI_draft.ts` (repo root) as the visual + interaction reference for this task. It establishes the palette (stone + emerald), shapes (soft rounded — `rounded-[1.8rem]`, `rounded-[2.5rem]`), typography (serif italic hero headers, sans body), iconography (lucide-react + custom MountainClimberIcon), kanban-column layout for Inbox/Today/This Week, drag-and-drop affordances, and motion (fade-in / slide-in). Reuse its Tailwind class patterns unless there is a clear reason to deviate. Pair with the `frontend-design` skill after loading the draft.

title: CL-13: Review / Daily Shutdown — completed list, carry-forward, reflection
description:
## Goal
Replace the F-06 Review placeholder with the Daily Shutdown ritual — show what got done today, walk unfinished items through carry-forward / drop / move, and capture an optional one-line reflection so the day ends cleanly.

## Scope
- `/review` route renders three sections, top to bottom:
  - **Completed today** — read-only list of tasks where `status='done'` AND `updated_at` is today; show count prominently ("You completed 7 things today")
  - **Unfinished today** — tasks where status='open' or 'in_progress' AND (due_at = today OR scheduled today); per-row actions:
    - **Carry forward** (default) — sets due_at to tomorrow; clears scheduled_*
    - **Drop** — sets status='dropped'
    - **Move to date** — date picker
    - **Done** — quick mark-complete in case the user forgot earlier
  - **Reflection** — optional single-line input "One word about today" or longer free-text (max 280 chars); saved to `daily_reflections` table (new migration `0010_daily_reflections.sql`)
- "Complete shutdown" button at bottom — sets `user_settings.last_shutdown_date = today`, navigates to Home, shows a calm closing toast ("Day closed.")
- "Skip shutdown" button — closes without writing reflection; does NOT mark last_shutdown_date
- Header shows date + total time focused today (sum of focus_session durations)
- Keyboard: `C` = carry forward selected, `D` = drop selected, `Enter` = complete shutdown

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Review/Review.tsx` (replace placeholder)
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Review/CompletedList.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Review/UnfinishedRow.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Review/ReflectionInput.tsx`
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/0010_daily_reflections.sql`
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/review.ts` — `review.summary()`, `review.carryForward(taskIds)`, `review.drop(taskIds)`, `review.saveReflection(text)`, `review.completeShutdown()`
- `shared/src/model/settings.ts` — extend with `last_shutdown_date`

## Acceptance
- With 7 done today + 3 unfinished today, the screen shows "7 completed" and 3 actionable rows
- Clicking "Carry forward" on an unfinished task sets due_at=tomorrow and removes it from today's view; verify via /plan tomorrow
- Saving reflection "long day" persists a row in `daily_reflections` with date=today and text="long day"
- "Complete shutdown" is a single transaction: writes reflection (if any), updates last_shutdown_date, navigates Home
- Reload after shutdown shows the same Completed list (history preserved)
- E2E test: full ritual — carry one, drop one, mark one done, save reflection, complete

## Notes
- AI tomorrow-suggestion (PRD §11) is Epic 7/8; no AI here.
- Time-focused total is computed from `focus_sessions` (CL-FOCUS) — show "—" if zero.
- Streaks / weekly review are post-MVP.

## References
PRD §11 Review, §7 item 6, §9 End of day.

title: CL-14: Empty states for the 5 PRD §13 states (first-open, inbox, plan, focus, review)
description:
## Goal
Implement the five PRD §13 empty states with calm, useful, ADHD-friendly copy and clear primary actions — replacing the placeholder strings left throughout Epic 2.

## Scope
The five states (PRD §13):
1. **First open with no items** — Home empty (no tasks, no inbox, no schedule)
   - Headline: "Welcome to Calmly. Capture anything to start."
   - Primary action: focus the CaptureBar (no scary onboarding wall)
   - Secondary: small link "Take the 60-second tour" (stub — full onboarding is in Epic 9; here just hide the link if the tour component doesn't exist)
2. **Empty inbox** — `/inbox` with zero unresolved items
   - Headline: "Inbox clear."
   - Sub: "Anything you capture will land here."
   - Action: Back to Home button + show the CaptureBar prominently
3. **Nothing scheduled today** — `/plan` and Home Today region with zero items
   - Headline: "Nothing on the schedule."
   - Sub: "Pick something from your backlog or capture a new task."
   - Actions: "Open backlog" + "Start ad-hoc focus"
4. **No current focus task** — `/focus` with no active session AND no candidates today
   - Headline: "No focus right now."
   - Sub: "Start an ad-hoc focus block, or pick from any open task."
   - Actions: "Start ad-hoc focus" + "Pick a task"
5. **Review with no completed items** — `/review` where today's done count is 0
   - Headline: "Some days are heavy. That's okay."
   - Sub: "You can still close out the day."
   - Action: "Complete shutdown" still available (no reflection required)

Implementation:
- Single `EmptyState` shared component takes `title`, `body`, `primaryAction`, `secondaryAction`
- Each consuming page checks its data and renders `<EmptyState />` when empty
- Tone guidelines: never accusatory ("you didn't do X"), never over-cheerful, never silent — every empty state explains what the user can do next
- Each empty state has a unique `data-empty-state="<name>"` attribute for E2E selectors

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/EmptyState.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Home/Home.tsx` (wire state 1, 3)
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Inbox/InboxList.tsx` (wire state 2)
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Plan/Plan.tsx` (wire state 3)
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Focus/Focus.tsx` (wire state 4)
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Review/Review.tsx` (wire state 5)

## Acceptance
- Fresh DB → open app → Home shows the first-open empty state with focused CaptureBar
- Manually clear inbox → /inbox shows "Inbox clear." state
- Day with no scheduled tasks → /plan shows "Nothing on the schedule."
- /focus with no active session AND no due_at=today tasks shows the no-focus state
- /review on a day with 0 completions shows the heavy-day state but Complete Shutdown still works

title: CL-15: Full daily-loop E2E test pass (Capture → Review)
description:
## Goal
Full daily-loop E2E test pass that exercises the deterministic core loop end-to-end: Capture → Inbox → Triage → Plan → Focus → Replan → Review. This is the MVP gating test for Epic 2 — if this passes, the deterministic shape of the product is provably working.

## Scope
- One Playwright spec `loop.spec.ts` that walks the full happy path:
  1. **Capture**: invoke global hotkey, type "buy birthday card", press Enter — verify InboxItem row created
  2. **Triage**: open `/inbox` triage focused mode → classify as task → set due_at = today → route to "Today" → next item
  3. **Plan**: navigate to `/plan` → drag the new task to the 14:00 slot → assert scheduled_at persisted
  4. **Focus**: from Home, click "Start focus" on the 14:00 task → assert FocusSession row created → click "Mark done" → assert task.status = 'done', session.ended_at set
  5. **Replan**: with one remaining unfinished task, open Replan from Focus → "Push to tomorrow" → assert due_at advanced
  6. **Review**: navigate to `/review` → assert "1 completed today" + "1 unfinished" → carry-forward unfinished → save reflection "long day" → complete shutdown → assert reflection persisted, last_shutdown_date set
- Negative-path mini-specs: capture without title (should reject), triage skip (item stays in inbox), Replan drop (task → status='dropped')
- Empty-state spec: fresh user → Home shows first-open empty state → capture flow still works
- CI integration: `e2e-core-loop` job depends on `e2e-foundations`

## Files
- `desktop/e2e/core-loop/loop.spec.ts` — the main happy-path spec

- `desktop/e2e/fixtures/seedUser.ts` — pre-signed-in fixture (reuses foundations fixture)

- The happy-path spec runs in under 60 seconds locally
- Each step uses semantic locators (role/name/testid), not nth-child or pixel positions
- Trace artifacts upload on failure
- Test isolation: each spec gets a fresh DB (truncate or new userData dir)

title: CL-02: Quick capture — input UI + global hotkey + persists to InboxItem
description:
## Goal
Implement the always-on quick capture: a persistent input UI in the AppShell, a global desktop hotkey, and an IPC path that persists raw text into `inbox_items` in under 5 seconds end-to-end.

## Scope
- Persistent **CaptureBar** component rendered by AppShell on every route
  - single-line text input + "Add" button
  - Enter submits; input clears; brief inline confirmation ("Added to Inbox")
- **Global hotkey** (default `CmdOrCtrl+Shift+I`) registered in main process via `globalShortcut`
  - When pressed, focuses the app window and focuses the CaptureBar
  - Shortcut is overridable from settings JSON (don't build the settings UI here — just read from `user_settings`)
- IPC handler `inbox.add(rawText: string, source: 'desktop')`
  - Inserts into `inbox_items` with `created_at = now()`, `resolved_at = NULL`
  - Returns the new item ID
- Optimistic UI: input clears immediately; if insert fails, restore text and surface inline error
- Trims whitespace; rejects empty strings; soft cap at 4000 chars (truncate + warn, do not silently drop)

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/components/CaptureBar.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/layout/AppShell.tsx` (add slot for CaptureBar)
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/inbox.ts` — `inbox.add` handler
- `desktop/src/main/shortcuts.ts` — global shortcut registration / unregister on app quit
- `desktop/src/preload/index.ts` — add `window.calmly.inbox.add`
- `shared/src/model/inbox.ts` — re-use existing schema

## Acceptance
- Typing "buy milk" + Enter creates a row in `inbox_items` with raw_text="buy milk", source="desktop"
- Pressing the global hotkey from another app focuses Calmly and places cursor in CaptureBar
- Submitting empty string is a no-op (no DB write, no error toast)
- Unit test: `inbox.add` rejects empty/whitespace, accepts valid strings, truncates at 4000 chars
- E2E test: type into capture bar, press Enter, assert toast + new inbox row visible on /inbox

## Notes
- AI parsing / brain-dump split is explicitly OUT of scope here (Epic 7).
- Global shortcut conflicts: if registration fails, log a warning; the in-app input still works. Settings UI to remap is in Epic 9.
- Voice capture is Telegram-only per PRD §8 — do not add a mic button.

## References
PRD §11 Capture, §7 item 2, §4 (low-friction principle).
notes:
LANDED: Full vertical slice complete and tested.

Implementation:
- main/inbox/store.ts: addInboxItem with trim → reject empty / truncate at 4000 → INSERT + enqueueOp inside one tx (6 tests, including FK-failure rollback path).
- main/auth/currentUser.ts: module-level cache + INSERT OR REPLACE INTO users mirror so the inbox_items.user_id FK resolves the moment a session is in hand (4 tests).
- main/ipc/inbox.ts: single 'inbox:add' handler. Reads currentUser, hardcodes source='desktop', returns NotSignedIn discriminant when no cached user.
- main/shortcuts.ts: registerCaptureHotkey('CmdOrCtrl+Shift+I'). Show + focus + send 'capture:focus'. Graceful failure path (returns {registered:false}); unregisterAllShortcuts on app.before-quit.
- main/index.ts: orchestrator wrapper now calls setCurrentUser on every redeem.ok / status / signOut. registerInboxIpc + registerCaptureHotkey wired in whenReady. Hotkey skipped when NODE_ENV=test so parallel e2e instances don't fight for the OS handler.
- preload/inbox.ts + api-types.ts: InboxBridge exposes add() + onFocusRequest(); CalmlyApi includes the new bridge.
- renderer/components/CaptureBar.tsx: persistent top-of-main bar. Optimistic clear, restore on failure, fades 'Added to Inbox' / 'Added (trimmed at 4000 chars)' confirmation after 1.8s, error states for EmptyInput/NotSignedIn/InternalError. Subscribes to onFocusRequest for the global hotkey.
- renderer/layout/AppShell.tsx: CaptureBar mounted above <Outlet/> inside <main>; Outlet wrapped in scrollable div so the bar stays pinned.
- e2e/foundations/capture.spec.ts: signs in → types → asserts inline toast → sync.syncNow asserts pushed>=1 (proves both local commit + op_queue happened atomically) → IPC truncation path.

Verified: typecheck clean (web + node), eslint clean on touched files, vitest 88/88 passing.
close_reason: Landed in 839ab46. Full vertical slice: persistent CaptureBar in AppShell, CmdOrCtrl+Shift+I global hotkey, inbox.add IPC, currentUser cache + users-table mirror (closes the FK gap that would have blocked every domain write). addInboxItem trims, rejects empty, truncates at 4000 chars, INSERTs and enqueues for sync atomically. 9 e2e tests pass (1.1m incl. testcontainer boot); 88 unit tests pass in 3.85s. Establishes the IPC validation + repo + atomic write+enqueue pattern that subsequent CL-* domain beads can copy.

title: CL-03: Inbox list view — browse, sort, snooze, skip
description:
## Goal
Replace the F-06 Inbox placeholder with a real browsable list view of unresolved inbox items, with sort, snooze, and skip controls — the "overview" surface complementing the focused triage view (CL-TRIAGE).

## Scope
- `/inbox` route shows all `inbox_items` where `resolved_at IS NULL`, newest first by default
- Per-row: raw_text (truncated at ~120 chars), created_at relative time, source badge (desktop/telegram-text/telegram-voice)
- Sort toggle: Newest / Oldest / Source-grouped
- Per-row actions:
  - **Triage** → routes to `/inbox/triage` focused on this item (CL-TRIAGE consumes the route param)
  - **Snooze** → sets `resolved_at = NULL` but adds `snoozed_until` field (add column in a new migration `0004_inbox_snooze.sql`); snoozed items hide until time elapsed
  - **Skip** → marks `resolved_at = now()` with no resolution (treated as discarded)
- "Triage all" button at top → routes to `/inbox/triage` (focused mode walks the queue)
- Empty state placeholder ("No inbox items") — full empty-state polish in CL-EMPTYSTATES
- Keyboard navigation: ↑/↓ to move selection, Enter to triage selected, S to snooze, X to skip

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Inbox/InboxList.tsx` (replace placeholder)
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Inbox/InboxRow.tsx`
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/0004_inbox_snooze.sql` — add `snoozed_until INTEGER NULL` to `inbox_items`
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/inbox.ts` — extend with `inbox.list`, `inbox.snooze`, `inbox.skip`
- `desktop/src/preload/index.ts` — extend bridge
- `shared/src/model/inbox.ts` — extend schema with snoozed_until

## Acceptance
- Seeded DB with 3 unresolved + 1 snoozed-future + 1 resolved item shows exactly 3 rows by default
- Snoozing an item for 1 hour removes it from the default list; advancing the clock past 1 hour brings it back
- Skipping an item sets resolved_at and removes it from the list permanently
- Keyboard: ↑/↓ moves selection visibly, Enter navigates to /inbox/triage?id=X
- Unit test: `inbox.list` query correctly filters snoozed items by current time

## Notes
- Triage classification + routing happens in CL-TRIAGE; this task only navigates there.
- Snooze duration picker UI: keep it simple — three preset buttons (1h, tomorrow, next week). No custom duration picker in MVP.
- Cross-device sync of snooze state is handled by F-11 sync protocol (already done at epic level).

## References
PRD §11 Triage (snooze/skip without penalty), §7 item 3, §10 Screen List.
notes:
LANDED: schema + store + IPC + UI all in place.

Schema. Desktop migration 0006_inbox_snooze.sql adds snoozed_until INTEGER + a partial WHERE-snoozed_until-IS-NOT-NULL index. Mirror pg-migration server/migrations/0004_inbox_snooze.cjs adds the same column on Postgres. server/src/sync/tables.ts now lists snoozed_until in the inbox_items columns array — without that, the server's apply.ts would silently drop the field on push. shared/src/model/inbox.ts schema adds snoozed_until: unixMs.nullable() with two new InboxItemSchema unit tests.

Store. desktop/src/main/inbox/store.ts grows three new helpers — listInbox(now), snoozeInboxItem(id, untilMs, now), skipInboxItem(id, now). Discovery during impl: the server's INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET col=EXCLUDED.col rule means a partial upsert payload nulls out every missing column. Snooze and skip therefore read the FULL row inside the same transaction and enqueue a complete snapshot. addInboxItem also gains snoozed_until: null in its sync payload for the same reason.

Today. countUnresolvedInbox(db, userId, now) now applies the same visibility predicate as listInbox so the Home InboxTriageCard count matches the rows on /inbox.

IPC. inbox:list, inbox:snooze, inbox:skip handlers behind window.calmly.inbox.{list,snooze,skip}. Each guards on getCurrentUser; renderer narrows on ok=false → NotSignedIn / NotFound / InvalidUntil.

UI. /inbox now shows the real list. InboxList.tsx orchestrates the keyboard model (↑/↓ to move selection, Enter to triage, S toggles a per-row snooze popover, X skips). InboxRow renders raw_text via line-clamp-2 (full text stays accessible to screen readers), source icon + relative time, three controls (snooze popover with 1h / tomorrow morning / next week presets, Skip, Triage). Sort toggle (Newest / Oldest / Source) re-sorts in memory. Empty / loading / signed-out / error states surfaced by the hook. /inbox/triage stub route accepts ?id=X so CL-04 can deep-link without re-fetching.

Verified: typecheck (web + node) clean, eslint clean on touched files, 219 tests passing total (desktop 118, server 37, shared 64). Full E2E with seeded inbox lives in calmly-tiy (depends on this + calmly-ttx for the shared seed fixture).

Closes 1 P0 blocker (CL-04 Triage). Skipped acceptance: full keyboard E2E + DB-seeded list rendering — moved to calmly-tiy so the seeded-DB fixture lands once and serves both Home + Inbox specs.
close_reason: Inbox list view + snooze/skip + IPC + schema (desktop+server) shipped. 219 tests pass; full DB-seeded E2E deferred to calmly-tiy.

title: CL-04: Triage focused mode — classify, due-date chips, route to Today/Week/Later
description:
## Goal
Build the focused triage mode: one inbox item at a time, classify its type, assign a date via quick chips, and route it to Today / This Week / Later by converting it into a Task (or Event, or discarding it).

## Scope
- Route `/inbox/triage` (optionally `?id=<itemId>` to start at a specific item)
- Walks unresolved inbox items in order; auto-advances on resolve
- Per-item card shows raw_text large + source + created_at
- **Type classifier** (radio/segment): Task | Event | Reference/Note (Note → discard for MVP, no Notes feature) | Discard
- **Title field** (editable; defaults to raw_text)
- **Due-date chips**: Today | Tomorrow | This Week (sets due_at to Friday this week) | Later (no due_at) | Pick date (date picker)
- **Route action buttons**: "Today" / "This Week" / "Later" — each creates the Task with the right due_at and sets `inbox_items.resolved_at = now()`
- For Event type: collects start_at/end_at via simple inputs and creates `events` row instead
- **Snooze** and **Skip** also available from this view (consistent with list view)
- Keyboard: 1=Task, 2=Event, 3=Discard; T=Today, W=This Week, L=Later; S=Snooze, X=Skip; Enter=Confirm
- After resolving, slide to next item; if queue empty, show "Inbox clear" celebratory state

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Inbox/TriageFocused.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Inbox/TypeClassifier.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Inbox/DueDateChips.tsx`
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/triage.ts` — `triage.resolveAsTask`, `triage.resolveAsEvent`, `triage.discard`
- `desktop/src/preload/index.ts` — extend bridge

## Acceptance
- With 3 unresolved items, opening /inbox/triage shows item 1; clicking "Today" creates a task with due_at=today, resolves item 1, advances to item 2
- Choosing "Discard" sets resolved_at without creating a task or event
- Choosing "Event" with start/end times creates a row in `events` and resolves the inbox item
- Keyboard shortcut `T` after typing in title field still routes to Today (shortcuts ignored while focus is in input — verify with E2E)
- After last item resolved, "Inbox clear" view renders with link back to Home
- Unit test: each `triage.resolve*` correctly creates the right entity and resolves the inbox item atomically (single transaction)

## Notes
- "Break it down" inline action lives in CL-BREAKDOWN — surface a placeholder "Break down" button here that CL-BREAKDOWN will wire up.
- AI suggestions for type/title/date/next-action are explicitly out (Epic 7).
- Reminder rule attachment happens in Epic 4; this task creates tasks without reminder_rules rows.

## References
PRD §11 Triage, §7 item 3, §9 Morning.
notes:
LANDED: triage focused mode — IPC + UI + tests all in place.

Store. desktop/src/main/triage/store.ts adds resolveAsTask, resolveAsEvent, discardInboxItem. All three share an atomic transaction: SELECT inbox row → INSERT task/event (skipped for discard) → UPDATE inbox.resolved_at + bump version → enqueue full-snapshot upserts for both rows. The shared loadInboxForResolve helper produces consistent NotFound vs AlreadyResolved discrimination. 10 unit tests cover empty-title rejection, NotFound, AlreadyResolved, full-snapshot enqueue contents, dueAt:null Later branch, end<start rejection on events, source='manual' on event inserts, discard skips entity creation, and InternalError on UPDATE failure.

IPC. desktop/src/main/ipc/triage.ts wires triage:resolveAsTask / triage:resolveAsEvent / triage:discard. Each guards on getCurrentUser; payload-shape validation rejects non-finite numbers and non-string ids before crossing into the store.

Bridge. preload/triage.ts + extended CalmlyApi.triage on api-types.ts surface TriageBridge.{resolveAsTask, resolveAsEvent, discard}. Wired into preload/index.ts.

UI. /inbox/triage replaces the prior stub: TypeClassifier (Task | Event | Discard radio with 1/2/3 keys), editable title field defaulting to raw_text, DueDateChips (Today | Tomorrow | This Week | Later | Pick date) for Task mode, datetime-local inputs for Event mode, primary actions (Today/This Week/Later for Task, Schedule for Event, Discard for Discard), Snooze popover (1h / Tomorrow morning / Next week) and Skip in the secondary group. Break-down placeholder surfaces but is disabled for CL-05. Keyboard model: 1/2/3 type, T/W/L date chip (Task only), S/X snooze/skip, Enter confirm primary; INPUT/TEXTAREA focus exempts shortcuts. Item card slides in via Tailwind animate-in keyframes when the cursor advances. 'Inbox clear' state celebrates with the MountainClimber icon + 'Back to today' button when the queue empties. Reuses InboxBridge.list (refresh after each resolution to slide forward) and InboxBridge.snooze/skip — no new IPC for those.

Date helpers. renderer/pages/Inbox/triageDates.ts (chipToday, chipTomorrow, chipThisWeek with Sat→next-Friday roll, endOfDay) — 7 unit tests including month-boundary crossings.

Verified: typecheck (web + node) clean, eslint clean on touched files, 135 vitest tests passing (was 118 before this bead). Full DB-seeded E2E lives in calmly-exi (CL-04-e2e, P1, depends on this + calmly-ttx for the seed fixture).

Closes 1 P0 + 1 P1 blocker (CL-09 Focus mode, CL-05 break-down inline).
close_reason: Triage focused mode — IPC + components + 17 new unit tests landed. 135 desktop tests pass; full DB-seeded E2E deferred to calmly-exi.

title: CL-05: Inline 'break it down' inside Triage (deterministic, no AI)
description:
## Goal
Add an inline "Break it down" action inside the focused Triage view that lets the user split a vague inbox item into a clearer next-action plus optional follow-up subtasks — fully deterministic (no AI), powered by manual user editing.

## Scope
- "Break down" button in CL-TRIAGE (already stubbed) opens an inline panel within the same triage card (no route change, no modal)
- Panel UI:
  - Original raw_text shown read-only at top
  - "Next action" text input — required, this becomes the resolved Task's title
  - "Also create subtasks" repeating-row list — each row is a free-text input + remove button + "Add row" affordance
- On confirm:
  - Creates one parent Task (the next action) with due_at from the chips
  - Creates child Tasks for each non-empty subtask row, with `parent_task_id` set to the parent and `due_at = NULL`
  - Resolves the inbox item with `source='manual-split'` recorded on each created task (use existing `source` field; add `'manual-split'` to the enum)
- "Cancel" closes the panel and returns to the regular triage card without resolving
- Keyboard: Enter in subtask row adds another row; Backspace on empty row removes it

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Inbox/BreakdownPanel.tsx`
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/triage.ts` — extend with `triage.resolveWithBreakdown(parent, subtasks[])`
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/0005_source_enum.sql` — relax/extend source CHECK to include `'manual-split'`
- `shared/src/model/task.ts` — add `'manual-split'` to source union + Zod schema

## Acceptance
- Opening Break down on an item, entering "email John" as next action and ["draft outline", "attach file"] as subtasks creates 3 tasks total: 1 parent + 2 children with correct `parent_task_id`
- Resolving via breakdown sets `inbox_items.resolved_at` once (single transaction; partial-failure rolls all back)
- Empty next-action input disables the Confirm button
- Empty subtask rows are silently skipped
- Unit test: `triage.resolveWithBreakdown` rolls back if any child insert fails

## Notes
- Explicitly NO AI here — this is the deterministic path. AI-powered "Make Startable" / brain-dump split is Epic 7.
- MVP UI exposes one level only (PRD §14); subtasks are stored but not visually nested in lists yet — they appear as standalone tasks. That's acceptable for this task.
- No reminder rules created on subtasks.

## References
PRD §11 Triage ("break a vague item into a clearer next action inline"), §14 (parent–child relationships from day one).

title: CL-06: Plan view — day grid with manual time blocks + drag/drop reorder
description:
## Goal
Replace the F-06 Plan placeholder with a real day-grid view where users can place tasks into time blocks manually and reorder them via drag/drop. No calendar import yet.

## Scope
- `/plan` route shows a single-day vertical grid (default = today; date picker for ±N days)
- Grid: 6:00 AM → 11:00 PM in 30-min slots (configurable later via settings; hardcode for MVP)
- Two columns inside the grid:
  - **Scheduled column** — placed time blocks (each block = a Task with `scheduled_start`, `scheduled_end`)
  - **Backlog column** — unplaced tasks for the selected day (Tasks with due_at on that day but no scheduled_start)
- Drag a backlog task onto a slot to place it (default 30-min duration)
- Drag a placed block to a different slot to reschedule (snaps to 15-min grid)
- Resize a block by dragging its bottom edge (15-min snap; min 15 min, max 4 h)
- Click a block to open a side panel with title, notes, due_at, scheduled_start/end editing
- Add new fields to `tasks`: `scheduled_start INTEGER NULL`, `scheduled_end INTEGER NULL` (migration `0006_task_schedule.sql`)
- Empty grid + empty backlog states placeholder ("Nothing scheduled today") — full polish in CL-EMPTYSTATES

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Plan/Plan.tsx` (replace placeholder)
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Plan/DayGrid.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Plan/TimeBlock.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Plan/Backlog.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Plan/TaskSidePanel.tsx`
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/0006_task_schedule.sql`
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/plan.ts` — `plan.listForDay`, `plan.schedule(taskId, start, end)`, `plan.unschedule(taskId)`
- `shared/src/model/task.ts` — add scheduled_start/scheduled_end (nullable)

## Acceptance
- A backlog task dragged onto the 9:00 AM slot creates a 30-min block at 9:00; DB row updated
- Dragging the block to 10:00 AM moves it; DB updated; refresh preserves the new position
- Resizing a block from 30 to 60 min updates scheduled_end correctly with 15-min snap
- Two blocks cannot occupy the exact same time range — overlap is allowed but visually flagged with a warning border
- E2E test: place a task → reload page → block still at expected slot

## Notes
- Calendar imports (Google/Microsoft events overlaid on the grid) are Epic 5 — leave room in the layout but don't implement.
- Reschedule controls beyond drag (move to date, push by hours) live in CL-PLAN-RESCHEDULE.
- Replan UI bulk operations live in CL-REPLAN.
- Use a small drag/drop lib (e.g., `@dnd-kit/core`); avoid HTML5 native DnD for keyboard/accessibility reasons.

## References
PRD §11 Plan, §7 item 4, §10 Screen List.
notes:
LANDED CL-06a (architectural piece): schema + IPC + bridge + types.

Schema. desktop migration 0007_task_schedule.sql adds scheduled_start/scheduled_end (nullable INTEGER) + partial index on (user_id, scheduled_start) WHERE NOT NULL. server migration 0005_task_schedule.cjs mirrors. server/src/sync/tables.ts adds both columns to tasks. shared/src/model/task.ts schema gains the pair-or-neither + end>=start refine; 3 new tests cover placed/half-placed/inverted-range.

Store. main/plan/store.ts: listForDay(now, tz) returns {scheduled, backlog} via two queries on the same local-day window — scheduled = open|in_progress with scheduled_start in window, backlog = same statuses with due_at in window AND no scheduled_start. scheduleTask + unscheduleTask both wrap UPDATE + full-snapshot enqueueOp in one tx so the server's EXCLUDED-based ON CONFLICT can't null out unrelated columns. Schedulability guard rejects done/dropped/snoozed silently as NotFound. 9 unit tests.

IPC. plan:listForDay({day?}) / plan:schedule({taskId, startAt, endAt}) / plan:unschedule(taskId). All guarded on getCurrentUser; payload-shape rejected before crossing into the store.

Bridge. preload/plan.ts + extended CalmlyApi.plan with PlanBridge.{listForDay, schedule, unschedule}. Wired into preload/index.ts.

Verified: typecheck (web + node) clean, eslint clean on touched files. Tests: desktop 144 (was 135; +9 plan/store), server 37, shared 67 (+3 task schema). 248 total.

title: CL-07: Plan reschedule controls — move-to-date, push-by, to-backlog
description:
## Goal
Add explicit reschedule controls to the Plan side panel (and any task row) — move to a different date, push by N hours, clear schedule — for keyboard-driven and bulk-friendly rescheduling without dragging.

## Scope
- Inside `TaskSidePanel` (CL-PLAN-GRID), add a "Reschedule" section with:
  - **Move to date** — date picker; preserves scheduled time-of-day if present
  - **Push by** — preset buttons: +30 min, +1 h, +4 h, +1 day; or numeric input + unit
  - **Move to backlog** — clears scheduled_start/scheduled_end (task remains; goes back to backlog)
  - **Drop from today** — clears due_at (and scheduled_*) — task returns to undated pool
- Right-click context menu on any time block in DayGrid offers same actions
- Right-click context menu on a backlog row offers: Move to date, Drop, Schedule for time…
- Each action emits a single transactional IPC call; UI updates optimistically + rolls back on error
- Keyboard shortcuts when a block/row is selected: `D` = move to date (opens picker), `+` = push by 1h, `Backspace` = move to backlog

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Plan/RescheduleControls.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Plan/TaskSidePanel.tsx` (extend)
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Plan/ContextMenu.tsx`
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/plan.ts` — add `plan.moveToDate`, `plan.pushBy`, `plan.toBacklog`, `plan.dropFromToday`

## Acceptance
- "Push by 1h" on a 9:00 AM block updates scheduled_start to 10:00 AM and scheduled_end correspondingly
- "Move to date" on a block at 9:00 AM today + selected tomorrow → block disappears from today's grid, appears at 9:00 AM tomorrow
- "Move to backlog" clears scheduled_* but preserves due_at; task appears in backlog column
- "Drop from today" clears due_at; task no longer in today's plan view at all
- Unit test: each IPC handler is a single transaction (verify with a fault-injection test that rolls back on simulated DB error)

## Notes
- Bulk multi-select reschedule (several blocks at once) is OUT — CL-REPLAN handles bulk via its own UI.
- Recurring task reschedule semantics (only this occurrence vs all future) are deferred — MVP treats each task as a single occurrence.

PRD §11 Plan ("reschedule quickly"), §11 Replan.

title: CL-08: Quick Plan ritual — morning confirm, reorder/drop/shrink today
description:
## Goal
Build the Quick Plan ritual — a morning-confirmation flow where the user reviews today's commitments and quickly reorders, drops, or shrinks them to fit a realistic day.

## Scope
- Triggered from Home (Quick Plan button) or auto-suggested first time the app opens each calendar day
- Modal (or full-screen sheet) titled "Quick Plan: <today's date>"
- Lists today's commitments in chronological order:
  - For each row: title, scheduled time (if any), duration estimate, three quick actions:
    - **Reorder** — drag handle to reorder (updates scheduled_start sequentially without overlaps)
    - **Drop** — moves to backlog (or "Drop from today" with confirmation)
    - **Shrink** — duration buttons (15m / 30m / 1h)
- Header shows total scheduled time today + count of commitments
- "Confirm day" button at bottom — closes the modal and writes any pending changes (changes apply optimistically as the user makes them; Confirm only closes)
- "Skip for today" button — closes without further changes; sets a flag so it won't re-prompt today
- Auto-suggest logic: on app launch, if `user_settings.last_quickplan_date != today` AND today has ≥1 commitment, open Quick Plan after a 1.5s delay (cancellable)

## Files

- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/QuickPlan/QuickPlanRow.tsx`

## References
PRD §7 item 7 (Quick Plan), §9 Morning, §11 Plan.

title: CL-09: Focus mode — current task + next step, soft time, mark done, switch task
description:
## Goal
Replace the F-06 Focus placeholder with a real focus mode UI: shows the current task plus its next step, exposes time as secondary info, supports mark-done, and lets the user switch tasks without leaving Focus.

## Scope
- `/focus` route renders the active focus session (if any); without a session, shows a chooser
- **Active session UI**:
  - Large current task title + parent task chain (if subtask)
  - "Next step" sub-line — for parent tasks, this is the first open child task; for leaf tasks, it's `notes` truncated to one line
  - Soft time visibility: scheduled time shown small + grey ("9:00 – 9:30"); elapsed timer optional and toggleable; no countdown by default
  - Primary action: **Mark done** — closes the task, advances to next scheduled item if any
  - Secondary actions: **Switch task** (opens picker), **I'm stuck** (opens guided prompts — CL-STUCK-PROMPTS), **End focus** (returns to Home)
- **Focus session state** persisted to `focus_sessions` table (new migration `0007_focus_sessions.sql`) — id, user_id, task_id, started_at, ended_at NULL, source ('scheduled'|'ad-hoc')
- **Switch task picker**: list of today's remaining tasks (scheduled + backlog), select one → ends current session, starts new
- Without an active session: Focus screen shows "Start focus" button + list of today's items to pick from (also handles ad-hoc — see CL-FOCUS-ADHOC)

## Files
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Focus/Focus.tsx` (replace placeholder)
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Focus/ActiveSession.tsx`
- `desktop/src/renderer/pages/Focus/SwitchTaskPicker.tsx`
- `desktop/src/main/db/migrations/0007_focus_sessions.sql`
- `desktop/src/main/ipc/focus.ts` — `focus.start(taskId, source)`, `focus.end()`, `focus.markDone()`, `focus.switch(newTaskId)`, `focus.current()`
- `desktop/src/preload/index.ts` — extend bridge
- `shared/src/model/focus.ts` — new file with FocusSession schema

## Acceptance
- Starting focus on a parent task with 2 open children renders title=parent, next-step=first child
- Mark done closes the active task (status='done') AND ends the focus session (`ended_at = now()`)
- Switch task ends current session, starts new one with a fresh started_at
- Reloading the app while a session is active resumes the same session
- Time display: scheduled time visible but small/grey; no countdown; toggle reveals elapsed timer
- E2E test: start focus, mark done, assert task status + session ended

## Notes
- "I'm stuck" prompts live in CL-STUCK-PROMPTS — surface a placeholder button here that CL-STUCK-PROMPTS will wire up.
- Ad-hoc focus blocks are CL-FOCUS-ADHOC; this task's "Start focus" picker shows only today's planned tasks.
- AI rescue suggestions are Epic 7/8.
- Notification suppression during focus (do not disturb) is Epic 4 (reminders).

## References
PRD §11 Focus, §7 item 5, §9 During the day.
notes:
LANDED CL-09a: schema + IPC for focus mode.

Schema. Desktop migration 0008_focus_sessions.sql creates a STRICT TABLE with id/user_id/task_id/started_at/ended_at/source. LOCAL ONLY — no server migration, no entry in syncTables. Side effects that DO sync (task.status='done' on markDone) flow through the regular tasks-upsert path with full-row snapshots. Two indices: partial open-sessions index for currentFocus's lookup; non-partial task_id index for cascading-delete affinity.

Shared. shared/src/model/focus.ts: FocusSourceSchema ('scheduled'|'ad-hoc') + FocusSessionSchema with end>=start refine. Re-exported from shared/src/model/index.ts.

Store. main/focus/store.ts:
- currentFocus(db, userId): single-row read of the open session.
- startFocus(db, userId, taskId, source, now): rejects unknown sources via InvalidArgs; rejects missing/non-schedulable tasks as NotFound; auto-ends prior open sessions in the same tx before INSERTing the new one.
- endFocus(db, userId, now): idempotent — returns ended:false when nothing was open.
- markDoneFromFocus(db, userId, now): in one tx — find open session, load task, UPDATE tasks.status='done' + version bump, enqueue full-snapshot tasks upsert, end the session. Returns NoActiveSession / NotFound / ok with the closed task's id.
- switchFocus(db, userId, newTaskId, source, now): end+start in one tx so the renderer never sees a 'no session' window.

13 unit tests cover currentFocus null/non-null, start with bad source / missing task / non-schedulable status / ends-prior-then-INSERTs ordering, end ended:false vs true, markDoneFromFocus NoActiveSession + happy-path with status flip + full-snapshot enqueue + session close, switchFocus bad source / missing task / ends-prior-then-INSERTs ordering.

IPC. window.calmly.focus.{current, start, end, markDone, switch} via main/ipc/focus.ts. Each guarded on getCurrentUser; payload-shape rejects bogus sources/ids before crossing into the store.

Bridge. preload/focus.ts + extended CalmlyApi.focus.

Verified. Typecheck clean (web + node). Eslint clean on touched files. 157 desktop tests pass (was 144; +13 focus/store). 67 shared tests pass. Server unchanged.

UI continues in calmly-fra (CL-09b, P0). Seeded-DB E2E in calmly-w0a (CL-09-e2e, P1, depends on calmly-fra + calmly-ttx).

Closes 1 P0 blocker (CL-13 Review).
close_reason: CL-09 architectural foundation (schema + IPC + bridge + 13 unit tests) landed. UI in calmly-fra; E2E in calmly-w0a.

title: F-14d: E2E persistence.spec.ts — sign in → quit → relaunch → still signed in (encrypted store survives)
description:
## Goal
Prove the encrypted session store survives an Electron restart.

## Scope
- desktop/e2e/foundations/persistence.spec.ts.
- Steps: sign in via F-14c helper → assert signed-in → app.close() → relaunch with the SAME --user-data-dir → assert signed-in again on cold boot (no re-auth).
- Cookie jar is persisted by Electron's session.defaultSession when user-data-dir is reused; this test guards that we don't accidentally clear it.

## Acceptance
- Spec passes; cleanup tears down the user-data-dir after both runs.

## Depends on
F-14a, F-14c
notes:
DESIGN: spec at desktop/e2e/foundations/persistence.spec.ts. Approach: server fixture beforeAll → tmp userDataDir created via mkdtemp → launchElectronApp({syncUrl, userDataDir}) → signInAsTestUser → dispose (leaves userDataDir intact since helper only deletes ones it created itself, by design) → second launchElectronApp with SAME userDataDir → on cold boot the renderer asks /auth/me with the persisted cookie → AuthProvider sees signed_in immediately → AuthGate skips SignIn and renders Home directly. Assert: 'Peace, friend.' visible without re-signing AND auth.status() returns the same user.email. Self-skip without Docker (mirrors auth.spec.ts).

NOT doing: the encrypted secret-store roundtrip across restart (separate concern; safeStorage is exercised by Home's main process selfTest at boot already and there's no F-14 child for that). Just session-cookie persistence.
close_reason: Landed in 5a4530e. Spec passes in 4.3-4.9s for the full restart flow (~14.8s incl. testcontainer boot). Watchdog races Home assertion vs. SignIn-visible to fail fast on regression. Self-skips without Docker.
